Iliac crest and iliac fossa (hip bone).name: Iliac crest and iliac fossa (hip bone)
Iliac crest and iliac fossa (hip bone).fact: The iliac crest is the superior border of the ilium (anchors quadratus lumborum); the iliac fossa is its concave inner surface (origin of iliacus).

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated region of the hip bone.
rel.explain: Iliacus arises from the iliac fossa; quadratus lumborum, latissimus dorsi, erector spinae and abdominal wall muscles attach to the iliac crest.

Psoas major.name: Psoas major
Psoas major.fact: Arises from T12-L5 bodies, discs and transverse processes and inserts on the lesser trochanter; flexes the hip with iliacus.

rel.q: What innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Anterior rami of L1 to L3
Anterior rami of lumbar spinal nerves
rel.explain: Psoas major receives direct branches from the anterior rami of L1-L3.

rel.q: On which bony landmark does the indicated muscle insert?
rel.explain: Psoas major joins iliacus to insert on the lesser trochanter.

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscle at the hip?
rel.explain: As part of iliopsoas, psoas major is the chief hip flexor.

Iliacus.name: Iliacus
Iliacus.fact: Fills the iliac fossa and joins the psoas tendon to insert on the lesser trochanter; flexes the hip.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Iliacus is supplied by the femoral nerve (L2-L4) in the iliac fossa.

rel.q: On which bony landmark does the indicated muscle insert?
rel.explain: Iliacus inserts with psoas major on the lesser trochanter.

Quadratus lumborum.name: Quadratus lumborum
Quadratus lumborum.fact: Runs from the iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament to the 12th rib and L1-L4 transverse processes; fixes the 12th rib in inspiration.

rel.q: What innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Anterior rami of T12 to L4
rel.explain: Quadratus lumborum is supplied by anterior rami of T12-L4.

rel.q: The indicated muscle attaches superiorly to which rib?
rel.explain: It inserts on the inferior border of the 12th rib, which it fixes during inspiration.

Trapezius.name: Trapezius
Trapezius.fact: Elevates, retracts and upwardly rotates the scapula; supplied by the spinal accessory nerve and transverse cervical artery.

rel.q: What nerve provides motor innervation to the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: CN XI supplies trapezius motor fibers; C3-C4 carry proprioception.

rel.q: Which artery is the main blood supply of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The transverse cervical artery, from the thyrocervical trunk, supplies trapezius.

Latissimus dorsi.name: Latissimus dorsi
Latissimus dorsi.fact: Extends, adducts and medially rotates the humerus; inserts on the floor of the intertubercular sulcus.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The thoracodorsal nerve (C6-C8) from the posterior cord supplies latissimus dorsi.

rel.q: Which cord of the brachial plexus gives rise to the nerve supplying the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The thoracodorsal nerve branches from the posterior cord.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts into the floor of which groove of the humerus?
rel.explain: Latissimus dorsi inserts on the floor of the intertubercular sulcus.

Levator scapulae.name: Levator scapulae
Levator scapulae.fact: Runs from C1-C4 transverse processes to the superior angle of the scapula; elevates the scapula and rotates the glenoid inferiorly.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Dorsal scapular nerve (C5) with contributions from C3-C4 cervical nerves.

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscle on the scapula?
rel.explain: As its name says, it elevates the scapula (and rotates the glenoid inferiorly).

Rhomboid major.name: Rhomboid major
Rhomboid major.fact: Runs from T2-T5 spinous processes to the medial border of the scapula below the spine; retracts the scapula.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The dorsal scapular nerve (C4-C5) supplies both rhomboids.

rel.q: Which artery supplies the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The dorsal scapular artery runs with the dorsal scapular nerve deep to the rhomboids.

Rhomboid minor.name: Rhomboid minor
Rhomboid minor.fact: Runs from the nuchal ligament and C7-T1 spinous processes to the medial scapular border at the root of the spine; retracts the scapula.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The dorsal scapular nerve (C4-C5) supplies rhomboid minor and major.

rel.q: Which artery supplies the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The dorsal scapular artery supplies levator scapulae and the rhomboids.

Serratus posterior superior.name: Serratus posterior superior
Serratus posterior superior.fact: Intermediate extrinsic back muscle from C7-T3 spinous processes to ribs 2-4; proposed rib elevator, likely mainly proprioceptive.

rel.q: What nerves innervate the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Serratus posterior superior is supplied by intercostal nerves 2-5 (anterior rami), not posterior rami.

Splenius capitis.name: Splenius capitis
Splenius capitis.fact: Runs from the nuchal ligament and C7-T3/T4 spinous processes to the mastoid process; extends the head and turns the face to the same side.

rel.q: What innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves
Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
Posterior rami of middle cervical spinal nerves
rel.show: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves
rel.explain: As an intrinsic back muscle it is supplied by posterior (dorsal) rami.

rel.q: Which bony process of the temporal bone does the indicated muscle insert on?
rel.explain: Splenius capitis inserts on the mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line.

Semispinalis.name: Semispinalis
Semispinalis.fact: Most superficial transversospinalis muscle; spans 4-6 segments and extends the head and thoracic/cervical spine.

rel.q: What innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Transversospinalis muscles are supplied by posterior rami.

rel.q: The indicated muscle belongs to which deep intrinsic back muscle group?
rel.explain: Semispinalis, multifidus and rotatores form the transversospinalis group.

Sternocleidomastoid.name: Sternocleidomastoid
Sternocleidomastoid.fact: Two heads (manubrium, medial clavicle) to the mastoid process; turns the face to the opposite side; supplied by CN XI.

rel.q: What nerve provides motor innervation to the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: CN XI supplies SCM motor fibers; C2-C3 carry proprioception.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts superiorly on which bony process?
answers: Mastoid process of the temporal bone
rel.explain: SCM inserts on the mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line.

Clavicle.name: Clavicle
Clavicle.fact: Strut holding the upper limb away from the trunk; most often fractured in its middle third.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates medially with which bone?
rel.explain: Medially it forms the sternoclavicular joint with the manubrium.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates laterally with which part of the scapula?
rel.explain: Laterally it forms the acromioclavicular joint.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated bone.
rel.show: Sternocleidomastoid, trapezius, deltoid or pectoralis major
rel.explain: SCM, trapezius, deltoid, pectoralis major and subclavius all attach to the clavicle.

Vertebral body and arch.name: Vertebral body and arch
Vertebral body and arch.fact: The weight-bearing body and the arch (paired pedicles + laminae) together enclose the vertebral foramen.

rel.q: What structure joins adjacent vertebral bodies?
rel.explain: Bodies are joined by intervertebral discs (symphyses).

rel.q: The vertebral arch is formed by the pedicles and which other paired parts?
rel.explain: Arch = paired pedicles + paired laminae.

Pedicle.name: Pedicle
Pedicle.fact: Short stout bar joining the arch to the body; its vertebral notches form the intervertebral foramina.

rel.q: The notches on adjacent indicated parts bound which opening?
rel.explain: Superior and inferior vertebral notches of adjacent pedicles form the intervertebral foramen.

rel.q: The indicated part connects the lamina to which part of the vertebra?
rel.explain: Pedicles attach the vertebral arch to the body.

Lamina.name: Lamina
Lamina.fact: Flat plate forming the posterior vertebral arch; removed in laminectomy; ligamenta flava connect adjacent laminae.

rel.q: Which ligament connects the indicated parts of adjacent vertebrae?
rel.explain: The elastic ligamenta flava join adjacent laminae.

rel.q: What surgical procedure removes the indicated part to decompress the spinal canal?
rel.explain: Laminectomy excises laminae (often with the spinous process) to access or decompress the canal.

Vertebral foramen.name: Vertebral foramen
Vertebral foramen.fact: Opening bounded by the body and arch of one vertebra; stacked foramina form the vertebral canal.

rel.q: What major neural structure passes through the indicated opening in the cervical and thoracic spine?
rel.explain: The vertebral foramen transmits the spinal cord and its meninges.

rel.q: The stacked series of the indicated openings forms what?
rel.explain: Successive vertebral foramina form the vertebral canal.

Spinous process.name: Spinous process
Spinous process.fact: Posterior projection from the junction of the laminae; palpable midline landmark and lever for back muscles.

rel.q: Name a ligament that attaches to the indicated process.
rel.explain: Supraspinous and interspinous ligaments connect spinous processes; the nuchal ligament is the cervical supraspinous ligament.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated process.
rel.explain: Spinous processes anchor superficial extrinsic back muscles and transversospinalis insertions.

rel.q: The indicated process projects posteriorly from the junction of which paired parts?
rel.explain: The spinous process arises where the two laminae meet.

Transverse process.name: Transverse process
Transverse process.fact: Lateral projection from the pedicle-lamina junction; thoracic transverse processes articulate with rib tubercles.

rel.q: In the thoracic region, the indicated process articulates with which part of a rib?
rel.explain: Costotransverse joints link transverse costal facets (T1-T10) with rib tubercles.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated process.
rel.show: Levator scapulae, quadratus lumborum or longissimus
rel.explain: Transverse processes anchor many muscles, including levator scapulae (C1-C4), quadratus lumborum (L1-L4) and transversospinalis.

Transverse foramen.name: Transverse foramen
Transverse foramen.fact: Opening in cervical transverse processes transmitting the vertebral artery (C6-C1) and vertebral veins.

rel.q: Which artery passes through the indicated opening?
rel.explain: The vertebral artery ascends through the transverse foramina of C6 to C1.

rel.q: The vertebral artery usually first enters the indicated opening at which vertebral level?
rel.explain: It typically enters at C6; the C7 foramen usually transmits only veins.

Vertebral artery.name: Vertebral artery
Vertebral artery.fact: First branch of the subclavian; ascends through C6-C1 transverse foramina and joins its partner to form the basilar artery.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
answers: First part of the subclavian artery
rel.explain: The vertebral artery is the first branch of the first part of the subclavian artery.

rel.q: The indicated artery joins its partner to form which artery?
rel.explain: Both vertebral arteries unite at the pontomedullary junction to form the basilar artery.

rel.q: The indicated artery enters the cranial cavity through which opening?
rel.explain: After crossing the suboccipital triangle it pierces the dura and passes through the foramen magnum.

Lumbar vertebra.name: Lumbar vertebra
Lumbar vertebra.fact: Largest vertebrae with kidney-shaped bodies and hatchet-shaped spinous processes; sagittal facets limit rotation.

rel.q: Which intrinsic back muscle attaches to the mammillary processes of the indicated vertebra?
rel.explain: Mammillary processes on lumbar superior articular processes anchor multifidus.

rel.q: Which movement is limited by the sagittal orientation of the indicated vertebra's facets?
rel.explain: Sagittally oriented lumbar facets permit flexion-extension but restrict rotation.

Atlanto-occipital joint: Occipital condy.name: Atlanto-occipital joint
Atlanto-occipital joint: Occipital condy.fact: Occipital condyles sit on the superior articular facets of the atlas; permits flexion-extension (nodding 'yes').

rel.q: What is the main movement at the indicated joint?
rel.explain: The atlanto-occipital joint allows nodding of the head.

Atlantoaxial joint: Axis (C2), Dens.name: Atlantoaxial joint
Atlantoaxial joint: Axis (C2), Dens.fact: Dens of C2 articulates with the anterior arch of the atlas, held by the transverse ligament; permits head rotation ('no').

rel.q: What is the main movement at the indicated joint?
rel.explain: The atlantoaxial joint provides about half of cervical rotation.

rel.q: Which ligament holds the dens against the anterior arch of the atlas?
rel.explain: The transverse ligament (part of the cruciate ligament) holds the dens in place.

Spinal nerve.name: Spinal nerve
Spinal nerve.fact: Mixed nerve formed by union of dorsal and ventral roots; exits the intervertebral foramen and divides into rami. 31 pairs.

rel.q: The indicated nerve exits the vertebral column through which opening?
rel.explain: Each spinal nerve leaves through an intervertebral foramen.

rel.q: How many pairs of the indicated nerves are there?
rel.explain: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal.

Dura mater.name: Dura mater
Dura mater.fact: Tough outermost meninx attached to the foramen magnum; the dural sac ends at S2.

rel.q: At what vertebral level does the sac formed by the indicated layer end?
rel.explain: The dural sac (with arachnoid) ends at S2.

rel.q: What space separates the indicated layer from the walls of the vertebral canal?
rel.explain: In the spine, epidural fat and venous plexus separate dura from bone.

Scapula.name: Scapula
Scapula.fact: Mobile triangular bone gliding on ribs 2-7; anchors the rotator cuff and forms the glenoid socket.

rel.q: The glenoid cavity of this bone articulates with which bone?
rel.explain: Glenoid cavity and humeral head form the glenohumeral joint.

rel.q: The lateral end of the clavicle articulates with which process of this bone?
rel.explain: The acromioclavicular joint joins the acromion and lateral clavicle.

Spine of scapula.name: Spine of scapula
Spine of scapula.fact: Ridge dividing the posterior scapula into supraspinous and infraspinous fossae; continues laterally as the acromion.

rel.q: The indicated ridge continues laterally as which process?
rel.explain: The scapular spine expands laterally into the acromion.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated bony ridge.
rel.explain: Trapezius inserts on the superior lip; spinal (posterior) deltoid arises from the inferior lip.

Supraspinous fossa.name: Supraspinous fossa
Supraspinous fossa.fact: Fossa above the scapular spine housing supraspinatus; suprascapular nerve and artery pass through it.

rel.q: Which muscle originates from the indicated fossa?
rel.explain: Supraspinatus arises from the supraspinous fossa.

rel.q: What nerve supplies the muscle occupying the indicated fossa?
rel.explain: Suprascapular nerve passes beneath the superior transverse scapular ligament to supply supraspinatus.

Infraspinous fossa.name: Infraspinous fossa
Infraspinous fossa.fact: Fossa below the scapular spine housing infraspinatus; reached by the suprascapular nerve via the spinoglenoid notch.

rel.q: Which muscle originates from the indicated fossa?
rel.explain: Infraspinatus arises from the infraspinous fossa.

rel.q: What nerve supplies the muscle occupying the indicated fossa?
rel.explain: Suprascapular nerve winds around the spinoglenoid notch to supply infraspinatus.

Acromion process.name: Acromion process
Acromion process.fact: Lateral end of the scapular spine forming the point of the shoulder; roofs the glenohumeral joint.

rel.q: The indicated process articulates with which bone?
rel.explain: It forms the acromioclavicular joint with the lateral clavicle.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated process.
rel.explain: Middle deltoid arises here; trapezius inserts here.

Coracoid process.name: Coracoid process
Coracoid process.fact: Hook-like anterior scapular process palpable below the lateral clavicle; anchors muscles and ligaments.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated process.
rel.explain: Pectoralis minor inserts; coracobrachialis and short head of biceps arise here.

Glenoid cavity.name: Glenoid cavity
Glenoid cavity.fact: Shallow socket of the glenohumeral joint deepened by the labrum; shallowness permits mobility but favors dislocation.

rel.q: The indicated surface articulates with which structure?
rel.explain: Glenoid and humeral head form the glenohumeral joint.

rel.q: What fibrocartilaginous rim deepens the indicated surface?
rel.explain: The labrum deepens the glenoid; SLAP and Bankart lesions tear it.

Humerus.name: Humerus
Humerus.fact: Arm bone; classic fracture-nerve pairs: surgical neck-axillary, midshaft-radial, supracondylar-median, medial epicondyle-ulnar.

rel.q: Proximally, the indicated bone articulates with which bone?
rel.explain: Humeral head articulates with the glenoid cavity of the scapula.

rel.q: A midshaft fracture of the indicated bone most commonly injures which nerve?
rel.explain: Radial nerve runs in the radial groove; injury causes wrist drop.

Head of humerus.name: Head of humerus
Head of humerus.fact: Hemispherical proximal articular surface of the humerus; anterior dislocation is most common.

rel.q: The indicated surface articulates with which structure?
rel.explain: Humeral head and glenoid cavity form the glenohumeral joint.

Trochlea.name: Trochlea
Trochlea.fact: Spool-shaped medial articular surface of the distal humerus forming the humeroulnar hinge.

rel.q: The indicated surface articulates with which bone?
rel.explain: Trochlea fits the trochlear notch of the ulna.

Capitulum.name: Capitulum
Capitulum.fact: Rounded lateral articular surface of the distal humerus forming the humeroradial joint.

rel.q: The indicated surface articulates with which bone?
rel.explain: Capitulum articulates with the radial head at the humeroradial joint.

Medial and lateral epicondyles.name: Medial and lateral epicondyles
Medial and lateral epicondyles.fact: Non-articular distal humeral projections: medial anchors the flexor-pronator origin and UCL; lateral the extensor-supinator origin and RCL.

Olecranon.name: Olecranon
Olecranon.fact: Proximal ulnar projection forming the point of the elbow; fits the olecranon fossa in extension.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated process.
rel.explain: Triceps inserts on the olecranon; anconeus attaches laterally.

rel.q: The indicated process belongs to which bone?
rel.explain: The olecranon is the proximal projection of the ulna.

Quadrangular space.name: Quadrangular space
Quadrangular space.fact: Bounded by teres minor, teres major, long head of triceps, and surgical neck of humerus.

rel.q: What nerve passes through the indicated space?
rel.explain: Axillary nerve exits the axilla through the quadrangular space.

rel.q: What artery passes through the indicated space?
rel.explain: It accompanies the axillary nerve through the space.

Glenohumeral joint.name: Glenohumeral joint
Glenohumeral joint.fact: Ball-and-socket joint; the most mobile and most often dislocated joint, usually anteroinferiorly.

rel.q: What type of synovial joint is the indicated joint?
rel.explain: Humeral head in the glenoid cavity forms a ball-and-socket joint.

rel.q: Which nerve is classically injured in anterior dislocation of the indicated joint?
rel.explain: The axillary nerve lies just inferior to the joint capsule.

Pectoralis minor.name: Pectoralis minor
Pectoralis minor.fact: Stabilizes, depresses, and protracts the scapula; divides the axillary artery into three parts.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Medial pectoral nerve (C8-T1) pierces and supplies pectoralis minor.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which scapular process?
rel.explain: Pectoralis minor runs from ribs 3-5 to the coracoid process.

rel.q: The indicated muscle divides which artery into three parts?
rel.explain: Parts 1, 2, 3 of the axillary artery are proximal, deep, and distal to pec minor.

Infraspinatus.name: Infraspinatus
Infraspinatus.fact: Laterally rotates the arm; rotator cuff stabilizer of the glenohumeral joint.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Suprascapular nerve reaches it via the spinoglenoid notch.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which humeral landmark?
rel.explain: It inserts on the middle facet of the greater tubercle.

Teres minor.name: Teres minor
Teres minor.fact: Laterally rotates and weakly adducts the arm; rotator cuff stabilizer.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Axillary nerve (C5-C6) supplies teres minor and deltoid.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which humeral landmark?
rel.explain: It inserts on the inferior facet of the greater tubercle.

Deltoid.name: Deltoid
Deltoid.fact: Acromial part abducts 15-90 degrees; clavicular part flexes and medially rotates; spinal part extends and laterally rotates.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Axillary nerve (C5-C6) supplies deltoid and teres minor.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which humeral landmark?
rel.explain: All three parts converge on the deltoid tuberosity.

Pectoralis major.name: Pectoralis major
Pectoralis major.fact: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; clavicular head flexes, sternocostal head extends the flexed arm.

rel.q: What nerves innervate the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Lateral (C5-C7) and medial (C8-T1) pectoral nerves.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which part of the intertubercular groove?
rel.explain: Pec major inserts on the lateral lip.

Teres major.name: Teres major
Teres major.fact: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; its inferior border marks the axillary-to-brachial artery transition.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Lower subscapular nerve (C5-C6) supplies teres major and lower subscapularis.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which part of the intertubercular groove?
rel.explain: Teres major inserts on the medial lip.

Roots of brachial plexus (C5–T1).name: Roots of brachial plexus (C5–T1)
Roots of brachial plexus (C5–T1).fact: Anterior rami of C5-T1 emerging between anterior and middle scalenes before uniting into trunks.

rel.q: Name a nerve that arises directly from the indicated structures.
rel.explain: Root branches: dorsal scapular (C5) and long thoracic (C5-C7).

rel.q: Which artery emerges with the indicated structures between the anterior and middle scalenes?
rel.explain: Plexus roots and the subclavian artery pass through the scalene interval.

Superior trunk.name: Superior trunk
Superior trunk.fact: Union of C5-C6; injury produces Erb palsy (waiter's tip).

rel.q: Which spinal nerve roots form the indicated trunk?
rel.explain: The superior trunk is the union of C5 and C6.

rel.q: Name a nerve that arises directly from the indicated trunk.
rel.explain: Superior trunk gives suprascapular and nerve to subclavius.

rel.q: Injury to the indicated trunk produces which named palsy?
rel.explain: Upper trunk injury gives the waiter's tip posture.

Middle trunk.name: Middle trunk
Middle trunk.fact: Continuation of the C7 root alone; divides into anterior (lateral cord) and posterior (posterior cord) divisions.

rel.q: Which spinal nerve root forms the indicated trunk?
rel.explain: The middle trunk is the C7 root alone.

Inferior trunk.name: Inferior trunk
Inferior trunk.fact: Union of C8-T1; injury produces Klumpke palsy (claw hand), e.g., from a cervical rib or Pancoast tumor.

rel.q: Which spinal nerve roots form the indicated trunk?
rel.explain: The inferior trunk is the union of C8 and T1.

rel.q: Injury to the indicated trunk produces which named palsy?
rel.explain: Lower trunk injury causes Klumpke palsy with claw hand.

Lateral cord.name: Lateral cord
Lateral cord.fact: Lies lateral to the 2nd part of the axillary artery; gives lateral pectoral, musculocutaneous, and lateral root of median.

rel.q: Name a nerve that arises from the indicated cord.
rel.explain: Lateral cord: lateral pectoral, musculocutaneous, lateral root of median.

rel.q: Which muscle lies superficial to the indicated cord, dividing the adjacent artery into parts?
rel.explain: Cords surround the 2nd part of the axillary artery deep to pectoralis minor.

Medial cord.name: Medial cord
Medial cord.fact: Lies medial to the 2nd part of the axillary artery; continues as the ulnar nerve.

rel.q: Name a nerve that arises from the indicated cord.
rel.explain: Medial cord: medial pectoral, medial cutaneous nerves, ulnar, medial root of median.

Posterior cord.name: Posterior cord
Posterior cord.fact: Formed by all three posterior divisions; gives upper and lower subscapular, thoracodorsal, axillary, and radial nerves (ULTRA).

rel.q: Name a nerve that arises from the indicated cord.
rel.explain: ULTRA: upper subscapular, lower subscapular, thoracodorsal, radial, axillary.

Musculocutaneous nerve.name: Musculocutaneous nerve
Musculocutaneous nerve.fact: Supplies coracobrachialis, biceps, brachialis; continues as the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve.

rel.q: Which cord of the brachial plexus gives rise to the indicated nerve?
rel.explain: Musculocutaneous (C5-C7) is a terminal branch of the lateral cord.

rel.q: Which muscle does the indicated nerve pierce?
rel.explain: It pierces coracobrachialis then runs between biceps and brachialis.

rel.q: The indicated nerve continues into the forearm as which cutaneous nerve?
rel.explain: It emerges lateral to the biceps tendon to supply lateral forearm skin.

Axillary nerve.name: Axillary nerve
Axillary nerve.fact: Supplies deltoid and teres minor and skin over the lateral shoulder; injured in surgical neck fracture or anterior dislocation.

rel.q: Which cord of the brachial plexus gives rise to the indicated nerve?
rel.explain: Axillary nerve (C5-C6) is a terminal branch of the posterior cord.

rel.q: Through which space does the indicated nerve leave the axilla?
rel.explain: It travels with the posterior circumflex humeral artery.

rel.q: Name a muscle innervated by the indicated nerve.
rel.explain: Axillary nerve supplies deltoid and teres minor.

Radial nerve.name: Radial nerve
Radial nerve.fact: Supplies posterior arm and forearm extensors; midshaft humeral fracture causes wrist drop.

rel.q: Which cord of the brachial plexus gives rise to the indicated nerve?
rel.explain: Radial nerve (C5-T1) is the largest posterior cord branch.

rel.q: In which humeral groove does the indicated nerve run?
rel.explain: It spirals in the radial groove with the deep brachial artery.

rel.q: Which artery accompanies the indicated nerve in the posterior arm?
rel.explain: Profunda brachii travels with it through the triangular interval and radial groove.

Median nerve.name: Median nerve
Median nerve.fact: Runs with the brachial artery without arm branches; supplies most forearm flexors and thenar muscles.

rel.q: Which cords of the brachial plexus form the indicated nerve?
rel.explain: Lateral and medial roots from the two cords unite to form the median nerve.

rel.q: Which artery accompanies the indicated nerve in the arm?
rel.explain: Median nerve crosses the brachial artery in the arm.

Ulnar nerve.name: Ulnar nerve
Ulnar nerve.fact: Supplies FCU, medial FDP, and most intrinsic hand muscles; injury causes claw hand.

rel.q: Which cord of the brachial plexus gives rise to the indicated nerve?
rel.explain: Ulnar nerve (C8-T1) is the terminal branch of the medial cord.

rel.q: The indicated nerve passes posterior to which humeral landmark?
rel.explain: It runs behind the medial epicondyle in the cubital tunnel (funny bone).

Thoracodorsal nerve.name: Thoracodorsal nerve
Thoracodorsal nerve.fact: Supplies latissimus dorsi; descends on the posterior axillary wall with the thoracodorsal artery.

rel.q: Which cord of the brachial plexus gives rise to the indicated nerve?
rel.explain: Thoracodorsal nerve (C6-C8) is a posterior cord branch.

rel.q: What muscle does the indicated nerve innervate?
rel.explain: Thoracodorsal nerve supplies latissimus dorsi.

Long head of biceps brachii.name: Long head of biceps brachii
Long head of biceps brachii.fact: Flexes elbow and supinates forearm; its tendon runs through the GH joint and intertubercular groove.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C6) supplies the biceps.

rel.q: The indicated muscle head originates from which scapular landmark?
rel.explain: Long head arises from the supraglenoid tubercle and superior labrum.

rel.q: In which humeral groove does the tendon of the indicated head run?
rel.explain: It is held there by the transverse humeral ligament.

Short head of biceps brachii.name: Short head of biceps brachii
Short head of biceps brachii.fact: Flexes elbow and supinates forearm; assists shoulder flexion.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C6) supplies the biceps.

rel.q: The indicated muscle head originates from which scapular process?
rel.explain: Short head arises from the coracoid tip with coracobrachialis.

Brachialis.name: Brachialis
Brachialis.fact: Main flexor of the elbow in all forearm positions.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Musculocutaneous nerve; a small lateral part gets radial fibers.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which bone?
rel.explain: It inserts on the coronoid process and ulnar tuberosity.

Coracobrachialis.name: Coracobrachialis
Coracobrachialis.fact: Flexes and adducts the arm; pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C7) pierces and supplies it.

rel.q: The indicated muscle originates from which scapular process?
rel.explain: It arises from the coracoid tip with the short head of biceps.

Long head of triceps brachii.name: Long head of triceps brachii
Long head of triceps brachii.fact: Extends elbow and extends/adducts arm; borders the quadrangular and triangular spaces.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Radial nerve (C6-C8) supplies all triceps heads.

rel.q: The indicated muscle head originates from which scapular landmark?
rel.explain: Long head arises from the infraglenoid tubercle.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which process?
rel.explain: All triceps heads insert on the olecranon.

Lateral head of triceps brachii.name: Lateral head of triceps brachii
Lateral head of triceps brachii.fact: Extends the elbow; strongest head for forceful extension; arises above the radial groove.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Radial nerve (C6-C8) supplies all triceps heads.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which process?
rel.explain: All triceps heads insert on the olecranon.

Elbow joint complex: Humeroulnar joint,.name: Elbow joint complex
Elbow joint complex: Humeroulnar joint,.fact: Hinge (humeroulnar, humeroradial) plus pivot (proximal radioulnar) joints sharing one capsule.

rel.q: Which ligament encircles the radial head at the indicated joint complex?
rel.explain: The annular ligament holds the radial head in the radial notch.

rel.q: Which nerve passes posterior to the medial epicondyle at the indicated joint?
rel.explain: Ulnar nerve runs in the cubital tunnel behind the medial epicondyle.

Ulnar collateral ligament.name: Ulnar collateral ligament
Ulnar collateral ligament.fact: Resists valgus stress; anterior band injured in throwing athletes (Tommy John repair).

rel.q: The indicated ligament attaches proximally to which humeral landmark?
rel.explain: UCL runs from medial epicondyle to coronoid and olecranon.

rel.q: The indicated ligament resists which stress at the elbow?
rel.explain: The medial ligament resists valgus (abducting) force, as in throwing.

Radial collateral ligament.name: Radial collateral ligament
Radial collateral ligament.fact: Resists varus stress; lateral elbow stabilizer blending with the annular ligament.

rel.q: The indicated ligament attaches proximally to which humeral landmark?
rel.explain: RCL runs from the lateral epicondyle to blend with the annular ligament.

rel.q: The indicated ligament resists which stress at the elbow?
rel.explain: The lateral ligament resists varus (adducting) force.

Annular ligament.name: Annular ligament
Annular ligament.fact: Encircles the radial head in the radial notch; radial head subluxation is nursemaid's elbow.

rel.q: The indicated ligament encircles which structure?
rel.explain: It holds the radial head against the radial notch of the ulna.

rel.q: The indicated ligament attaches to the margins of a notch on which bone?
rel.explain: It attaches to anterior and posterior margins of the ulna's radial notch.

Subclavian artery.name: Subclavian artery
Subclavian artery.fact: Supplies upper limb, brain (vertebral), neck, and thoracic wall; passes between anterior and middle scalenes.

rel.q: At the lateral border of the 1st rib, the indicated artery becomes which artery?
rel.explain: Subclavian becomes axillary at the 1st rib's lateral border.

rel.q: Which muscle passes anterior to the indicated artery, dividing it into three parts?
rel.explain: The artery runs posterior to anterior scalene, between it and middle scalene.

Axillary artery.name: Axillary artery
Axillary artery.fact: Runs from the 1st rib to teres major; pectoralis minor divides it into three parts.

rel.q: What does the indicated artery become after it passes the inferior border of teres major?
rel.explain: Axillary becomes brachial at the inferior border of teres major.

rel.q: What artery immediately precedes the indicated artery?
rel.explain: Subclavian becomes axillary at the lateral border of the 1st rib.

rel.q: Which muscle divides the indicated artery into three parts?
rel.explain: Parts 1-3 lie proximal, deep, and distal to pectoralis minor.

Subscapular artery.name: Subscapular artery
Subscapular artery.fact: Largest axillary branch (3rd part); supplies subscapularis, latissimus, teres major; key scapular anastomosis contributor.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: It arises from the 3rd part of the axillary artery.

rel.q: Name a branch of the indicated artery.
rel.explain: It divides into circumflex scapular and thoracodorsal arteries.

Anterior circumflex humeral artery.name: Anterior circumflex humeral artery
Anterior circumflex humeral artery.fact: From the 3rd part of the axillary; winds anterior to the surgical neck to supply the humeral head.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: It arises from the 3rd part of the axillary artery.

rel.q: The indicated artery anastomoses with which artery around the surgical neck?
rel.explain: The two circumflex humerals encircle the surgical neck.

Posterior circumflex humeral artery.name: Posterior circumflex humeral artery
Posterior circumflex humeral artery.fact: From the 3rd part of the axillary; supplies deltoid, teres minor, GH joint; injured in surgical neck fracture.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: It arises from the 3rd part of the axillary artery.

rel.q: Through which space does the indicated artery pass?
rel.explain: It passes through the quadrangular space.

rel.q: Which nerve accompanies the indicated artery?
rel.explain: Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery travel together.

Brachial artery.name: Brachial artery
Brachial artery.fact: Main artery of the arm, supplying the anterior compartment; site of blood pressure measurement.

rel.q: What artery immediately precedes the indicated artery?
rel.explain: Axillary becomes brachial at the inferior border of teres major.

rel.q: Name a terminal branch of the indicated artery.
rel.explain: It divides into radial and ulnar arteries in the cubital fossa.

rel.q: Which nerve accompanies the indicated artery in the arm?
rel.explain: Median nerve runs with the brachial artery in the arm.

Deep brachial artery (profunda brachii).name: Deep brachial artery (profunda brachii)
Deep brachial artery (profunda brachii).fact: Supplies the posterior compartment (triceps); contributes to the elbow anastomosis via collateral arteries.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: It is an early branch of the proximal brachial artery.

rel.q: Which nerve accompanies the indicated artery?
rel.explain: Deep brachial artery travels with the radial nerve.

rel.q: In which humeral groove does the indicated artery run?
rel.explain: It runs in the radial groove with the radial nerve.

Brachial veins.name: Brachial veins
Brachial veins.fact: Paired venae comitantes accompanying the brachial artery and draining deep arm structures.

rel.q: The indicated veins join which superficial vein to form the axillary vein?
rel.explain: Brachial veins plus basilic vein form the axillary vein.

rel.q: The indicated veins accompany which artery?
rel.explain: They are venae comitantes of the brachial artery.

Basilic vein.name: Basilic vein
Basilic vein.fact: Superficial vein draining medial hand, forearm, and arm; pierces deep fascia mid-arm.

rel.q: The indicated vein joins the brachial veins to form which vein?
rel.explain: Basilic plus brachial veins form the axillary vein at teres major.

Cephalic vein.name: Cephalic vein
Cephalic vein.fact: Superficial vein draining lateral hand, forearm, and arm; runs in the deltopectoral groove.

rel.q: The indicated vein drains into which vein?
rel.explain: It pierces the clavipectoral fascia to enter the axillary vein.

rel.q: The indicated vein ascends in which groove at the shoulder?
rel.explain: It runs between deltoid and pectoralis major.

Axillary vein.name: Axillary vein
Axillary vein.fact: Drains upper limb, axilla, and lateral thoracic wall; lies medial to the axillary artery.

rel.q: At the lateral border of the 1st rib, the indicated vein becomes which vein?
rel.explain: Axillary vein becomes subclavian at the 1st rib.

rel.q: Name a vein that joins to form the indicated vein.
rel.explain: Basilic and brachial veins unite at teres major.

Subclavian vein.name: Subclavian vein
Subclavian vein.fact: Drains the upper limb; passes anterior to anterior scalene; common central venous access site.

rel.q: The indicated vein joins the internal jugular vein to form which vein?
rel.explain: Subclavian plus internal jugular form the brachiocephalic vein.

rel.q: What vein immediately precedes the indicated vein?
rel.explain: Axillary vein becomes subclavian at the lateral border of the 1st rib.

rel.q: The indicated vein passes anterior to which muscle?
rel.explain: The vein lies anterior, the artery posterior, to anterior scalene.

Radius.name: Radius
Radius.fact: Lateral forearm bone that rotates around the ulna in pronation/supination and forms the main wrist articulation; distal fracture = Colles.

rel.q: Name a carpal bone that articulates with the distal end of the indicated bone.
rel.explain: The distal radius (with the articular disc) articulates with the scaphoid and lunate at the radiocarpal joint.

rel.q: The proximal end of the indicated bone articulates with which part of the humerus?
rel.explain: The radial head articulates with the capitulum of the humerus.

Ulna.name: Ulna
Ulna.fact: Medial forearm bone forming the stable hinge at the elbow via its trochlear notch.

rel.q: The trochlear notch of the indicated bone articulates with which part of the humerus?
rel.explain: The ulna's trochlear notch wraps the humeral trochlea, forming the elbow hinge.

Head of radius.name: Head of radius
Head of radius.fact: Disc-shaped proximal radius that spins within the annular ligament during pronation/supination.

rel.q: Which ligament encircles the indicated structure?
rel.explain: The annular ligament holds the radial head against the radial notch of the ulna.

rel.q: The indicated structure articulates with which part of the humerus?
rel.explain: The radial head articulates superiorly with the capitulum.

Radial tuberosity.name: Radial tuberosity
Radial tuberosity.fact: Medial projection below the radial neck; lever point for supination.

rel.q: Which muscle inserts on the indicated landmark?
rel.explain: The biceps brachii tendon inserts on the radial tuberosity, making it a powerful supinator.

Ulnar notch of radius.name: Ulnar notch of radius
Ulnar notch of radius.fact: Concavity on the medial distal radius that receives the ulnar head at the distal radioulnar joint.

rel.q: The indicated structure articulates with which part of the ulna?
rel.explain: The ulnar notch receives the head of the ulna.

rel.q: The indicated structure forms part of which joint?
rel.explain: Ulnar notch plus ulnar head form the distal radioulnar pivot joint.

Styloid process of radius.name: Styloid process of radius
Styloid process of radius.fact: Lateral distal radial projection extending farther distally than the ulnar styloid; palpable at the proximal snuffbox.

rel.q: Which muscle inserts at the base of the indicated landmark?
rel.explain: Brachioradialis runs from the lateral supracondylar ridge to the base of the radial styloid.

Scaphoid.name: Scaphoid
Scaphoid.fact: Most commonly fractured carpal; retrograde blood supply risks proximal pole avascular necrosis or nonunion.

rel.q: The indicated bone forms the floor of which space?
rel.explain: Scaphoid (and trapezium) form the snuffbox floor; snuffbox tenderness suggests scaphoid fracture.

rel.q: Which artery supplies the indicated bone via branches entering distally?
rel.explain: Radial artery branches enter distally and flow retrograde, so proximal pole fractures risk avascular necrosis.

Lunate.name: Lunate
Lunate.fact: Most commonly dislocated carpal; anterior dislocation compresses the median nerve in the carpal tunnel.

rel.q: Anterior dislocation of the indicated bone compresses which nerve?
rel.explain: The anteriorly displaced lunate encroaches on the carpal tunnel, compressing the median nerve.

Triquetrum.name: Triquetrum
Triquetrum.fact: Pyramidal medial bone of the proximal carpal row; separated from the ulna by the articular disc.

rel.q: Which sesamoid carpal bone articulates with the palmar surface of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: The pisiform sits on the palmar surface of the triquetrum.

Pisiform.name: Pisiform
Pisiform.fact: Sesamoid bone in the FCU tendon; forms the medial wall of Guyon's canal.

rel.q: The indicated bone is a sesamoid within the tendon of which muscle?
rel.explain: The pisiform develops within the FCU tendon, which inserts on it.

rel.q: The indicated bone forms the medial wall of which canal?
rel.explain: Guyon's canal lies between the pisiform (medial) and hook of hamate (lateral).

rel.q: Which hypothenar muscle originates from the indicated bone?
rel.explain: Abductor digiti minimi arises from the pisiform and FCU tendon.

Trapezium.name: Trapezium
Trapezium.fact: Forms the saddle-shaped thumb CMC joint; its groove transmits the FCR tendon.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates with the base of which metacarpal to form a saddle joint?
rel.explain: Trapezium plus base of metacarpal I form the saddle-shaped thumb CMC joint.

rel.q: Which tendon runs in the groove of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: The FCR tendon travels in the trapezium groove toward the base of metacarpal II.

Trapezoid.name: Trapezoid
Trapezoid.fact: Smallest, wedge-shaped bone of the distal carpal row.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates distally with which metacarpal?
rel.explain: The trapezoid articulates with the base of the 2nd metacarpal.

Capitate.name: Capitate
Capitate.fact: Largest carpal and first to ossify; keystone of the carpal arch.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates distally mainly with which metacarpal?
rel.explain: The capitate articulates chiefly with the base of the 3rd metacarpal.

Hamate.name: Hamate
Hamate.fact: Its hook forms the lateral wall of Guyon's canal; hook fracture can injure the ulnar nerve.

rel.q: The hook of the indicated bone forms the lateral wall of which canal?
rel.explain: Guyon's canal lies between the pisiform and the hook of hamate.

rel.q: Fracture of the hook of the indicated bone can injure which nerve?
rel.explain: The ulnar nerve passes through Guyon's canal beside the hook of hamate.

rel.q: Name a metacarpal that articulates with the indicated bone.
rel.explain: The hamate articulates with the bases of metacarpals IV and V.

Metacarpal I.name: Metacarpal I
Metacarpal I.fact: Shortest, thickest metacarpal; its mobile saddle joint permits thumb opposition.

rel.q: The base of the indicated bone articulates with which carpal bone?
rel.explain: Trapezium and base of metacarpal I form the saddle CMC joint of the thumb.

rel.q: Which forearm muscle inserts on the base of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: APL inserts on the base of the 1st metacarpal.

Metacarpal II.name: Metacarpal II
Metacarpal II.fact: Longest metacarpal with a nearly immobile CMC joint; ECRL and FCR insert on its base.

rel.q: Name a muscle that inserts on the base of the indicated bone.
rel.explain: ECRL inserts dorsally and FCR palmarly on the base of the 2nd metacarpal.

rel.q: The base of the indicated bone articulates mainly with which carpal bone?
rel.explain: The 2nd metacarpal base sits mainly on the trapezoid.

Metacarpal III.name: Metacarpal III
Metacarpal III.fact: Has a styloid process at its base; central axis of the hand for abduction/adduction.

rel.q: Which wrist extensor inserts on the base of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: ECRB inserts on the dorsal base of the 3rd metacarpal.

rel.q: The base of the indicated bone articulates with which carpal bone?
rel.explain: The 3rd metacarpal base articulates with the capitate.

Metacarpal IV.name: Metacarpal IV
Metacarpal IV.fact: Slender metacarpal with a slightly mobile CMC joint.

rel.q: Name a carpal bone that articulates with the base of the indicated bone.
rel.explain: The 4th metacarpal base articulates with the hamate and capitate.

Metacarpal V.name: Metacarpal V
Metacarpal V.fact: Most mobile medial metacarpal; neck fracture is a boxer's fracture.

rel.q: The base of the indicated bone articulates with which carpal bone?
rel.explain: The 5th metacarpal base articulates with the hamate.

rel.q: Which wrist extensor inserts on the base of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: ECU inserts on the base of the 5th metacarpal.

rel.q: Fracture of the neck of the indicated bone is known by what eponym?
rel.explain: Punching a hard object classically fractures the 5th metacarpal neck.

Proximal phalanges.name: Proximal phalanges
Proximal phalanges.fact: Bases articulate with metacarpal heads at the MCP joints; heads articulate with middle phalanges (thumb: distal).

rel.q: The bases of the indicated bones form which joints?
rel.explain: Proximal phalanx bases articulate with metacarpal heads at the MCP joints.

Middle phalanges.name: Middle phalanges
Middle phalanges.fact: Present in digits 2-5 only, between the PIP and DIP joints; FDS inserts on their sides.

rel.q: Which forearm muscle inserts on the sides of the indicated bones?
rel.explain: Split FDS tendons insert on the shafts of the middle phalanges of digits 2-5.

Distal phalanges.name: Distal phalanges
Distal phalanges.fact: Terminal phalanges supporting the nail bed and pulp; FDP (digits 2-5) and FPL (thumb) insert on their palmar bases.

rel.q: Name a long flexor muscle that inserts on the palmar base of the indicated bones.
rel.explain: FDP inserts on distal phalanges of digits 2-5; FPL on the thumb's distal phalanx.

Radiocarpal (wrist) joint.name: Radiocarpal (wrist) joint
Radiocarpal (wrist) joint.fact: Condyloid synovial joint between the distal radius/articular disc and the scaphoid, lunate, and triquetrum.

rel.q: Name a carpal bone that participates in the indicated joint.
rel.explain: The proximal row (except pisiform) articulates with the radius and articular disc.

rel.q: What type of synovial joint is the indicated joint?
rel.explain: It allows flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, and circumduction but not rotation.

Flexor retinaculum.name: Flexor retinaculum
Flexor retinaculum.fact: Roof of the carpal tunnel, spanning scaphoid/trapezium tubercles to pisiform/hook of hamate; divided in carpal tunnel release.

rel.q: The indicated structure forms the roof of which space?
rel.explain: Carpal bones form the floor and walls; the flexor retinaculum forms the roof.

rel.q: Which nerve passes deep to the indicated structure?
rel.explain: The median nerve runs through the carpal tunnel beneath the flexor retinaculum.

rel.q: Name a bone to which the indicated structure attaches.
rel.explain: It spans scaphoid and trapezium tubercles laterally to the pisiform and hook of hamate medially.

Carpal tunnel.name: Carpal tunnel
Carpal tunnel.fact: Transmits the median nerve and 9 tendons (4 FDS, 4 FDP, FPL); compression causes carpal tunnel syndrome.

rel.q: Which nerve passes through the indicated space?
rel.explain: Median nerve compression here causes carpal tunnel syndrome.

rel.q: Name a muscle whose tendon passes through the indicated space.
rel.explain: Four FDS, four FDP, and the FPL tendon pass through the tunnel.

rel.q: What structure forms the roof of the indicated space?
rel.explain: Carpal bones form floor and walls; the flexor retinaculum forms the roof.

Pronator teres.name: Pronator teres
Pronator teres.fact: Pronates the forearm and weakly flexes the elbow; the median nerve passes between its two heads.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Pronator teres is supplied by the median nerve (C6-C7).

rel.q: Which nerve passes between the two heads of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The median nerve enters the forearm between the humeral and ulnar heads.

Flexor carpi radialis.name: Flexor carpi radialis
Flexor carpi radialis.fact: Flexes and abducts (radially deviates) the wrist; inserts on the base of the 2nd metacarpal.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FCR is supplied by the median nerve (C6-C7).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on the base of which metacarpal?
rel.explain: FCR runs through the trapezium groove to the base of metacarpal II.

Palmaris longus.name: Palmaris longus
Palmaris longus.fact: Weak wrist flexor that tenses the palmar aponeurosis; absent in ~14%; common tendon graft source.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Palmaris longus is supplied by the median nerve (C7-C8).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts into which fascial structure of the palm?
rel.explain: Its tendon passes superficial to the flexor retinaculum into the palmar aponeurosis.

Flexor carpi ulnaris.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
Flexor carpi ulnaris.fact: Flexes and adducts (ulnar deviates) the wrist; the ulnar nerve enters the forearm between its heads.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FCU is one of only 1.5 anterior forearm muscles supplied by the ulnar nerve.

rel.q: Which sesamoid bone lies within the tendon of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FCU inserts on the pisiform, then via ligaments to hook of hamate and 5th metacarpal.

Flexor digitorum superficialis.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis
Flexor digitorum superficialis.fact: Flexes the PIP joints of digits 2-5 (also MCP and wrist); inserts on the middle phalanges.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FDS is supplied by the median nerve (C7-T1).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which phalanges?
rel.explain: Its split tendons insert on the shafts of the middle phalanges of digits 2-5.

Flexor digitorum profundus.name: Flexor digitorum profundus
Flexor digitorum profundus.fact: Only muscle flexing the DIP joints of digits 2-5; dual innervation (ulnar medial half, AIN lateral half).

rel.q: What nerve innervates the lateral (radial) half of the indicated muscle?
answers: Anterior interosseous branch of median nerve
rel.explain: Lateral FDP (digits 2-3) is supplied by the AIN branch of the median nerve.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the medial (ulnar) half of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Medial FDP (digits 4-5) is supplied by the ulnar nerve.

rel.q: Which intrinsic hand muscles originate from the tendons of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The four lumbricals arise from the FDP tendons in the palm.

Flexor pollicis longus.name: Flexor pollicis longus
Flexor pollicis longus.fact: Flexes the thumb at the IP joint (and MCP); inserts on the base of the thumb's distal phalanx.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Anterior interosseous branch of median nerve
rel.explain: FPL is supplied by the AIN (C8-T1); AIN lesion prevents the OK sign.

Pronator quadratus.name: Pronator quadratus
Pronator quadratus.fact: Prime pronator of the forearm; binds the distal radius and ulna together.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Anterior interosseous branch of median nerve
rel.explain: Pronator quadratus is supplied by the AIN (C8-T1).

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: It is the prime pronator, pulling the distal radius over the ulna.

Brachioradialis.name: Brachioradialis
Brachioradialis.fact: Flexes the elbow, strongest in the midprone (thumb-up) position; inserts at the base of the radial styloid.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Despite flexing the elbow, brachioradialis is supplied by the radial nerve (C5-C6).

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: It flexes the elbow, most strongly with the forearm midprone.

Extensor carpi radialis longus.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus
Extensor carpi radialis longus.fact: Extends and abducts the wrist; key for fist clenching; inserts on dorsal base of the 2nd metacarpal.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: ECRL is supplied directly by the radial nerve (C6-C7) before it divides.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on the base of which metacarpal?
rel.explain: ECRL inserts on the dorsal base of metacarpal II.

Extensor carpi radialis brevis.name: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
Extensor carpi radialis brevis.fact: Extends and abducts the wrist; its origin is implicated in lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow).

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Deep branch of the radial nerve
rel.explain: ECRB is supplied by the deep branch of the radial nerve (C7-C8).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on the base of which metacarpal?
rel.explain: ECRB inserts on the dorsal base of metacarpal III.

Extensor digitorum.name: Extensor digitorum
Extensor digitorum.fact: Extends digits 2-5 at the MCP (IPs via extensor expansions) and assists wrist extension.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: ED is supplied by the PIN (C7-C8), continuation of the deep radial nerve.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts into what structures on digits 2-5?
rel.explain: ED tendons form the extensor expansions (hoods) of digits 2-5.

Extensor digiti minimi.name: Extensor digiti minimi
Extensor digiti minimi.fact: Extends the 5th digit via its extensor expansion.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: EDM is supplied by the PIN (C7-C8).

rel.q: The indicated muscle extends which digit?
rel.explain: It inserts on the extensor expansion of the 5th digit.

Extensor carpi ulnaris.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris
Extensor carpi ulnaris.fact: Extends and adducts (ulnar deviates) the wrist; inserts on base of the 5th metacarpal.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: ECU is supplied by the PIN (C7-C8).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on the base of which metacarpal?
rel.explain: ECU inserts on the base of metacarpal V.

Supinator.name: Supinator
Supinator.fact: Main supinator when the elbow is extended; the deep radial nerve pierces it (arcade of Frohse) to become the PIN.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Deep branch of the radial nerve
rel.explain: The deep radial branch supplies supinator as it passes through it.

rel.q: The nerve that pierces the indicated muscle continues as which nerve?
rel.explain: After passing through supinator, the deep radial branch is called the PIN.

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: It supinates, especially with the elbow extended when biceps is weak.

Abductor pollicis longus.name: Abductor pollicis longus
Abductor pollicis longus.fact: Abducts and extends the thumb at the CMC; forms the lateral snuffbox border; involved in de Quervain tenosynovitis.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: APL is supplied by the PIN (C7-C8).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on the base of which bone?
rel.explain: APL inserts on the base of the 1st metacarpal.

rel.q: Tenosynovitis of the indicated muscle's tendon (with EPB) is known by what eponym?
rel.explain: APL and EPB share the 1st dorsal compartment, where they become inflamed.

Extensor pollicis brevis.name: Extensor pollicis brevis
Extensor pollicis brevis.fact: Extends the thumb at the MCP; lateral snuffbox border; involved with APL in de Quervain tenosynovitis.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: EPB is supplied by the PIN (C7-C8).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on the base of which bone?
rel.explain: EPB inserts on the base of the thumb's proximal phalanx, extending the MCP.

Extensor pollicis longus.name: Extensor pollicis longus
Extensor pollicis longus.fact: Extends the thumb at the IP (and MCP, CMC); hooks around the dorsal (Lister) tubercle; medial snuffbox border.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: EPL is supplied by the PIN (C7-C8).

rel.q: The tendon of the indicated muscle hooks around which bony landmark of the radius?
rel.explain: EPL uses Lister's tubercle as a pulley to redirect toward the thumb.

rel.q: The indicated muscle's tendon forms the medial border of which space?
rel.explain: EPL bounds the snuffbox medially; APL and EPB laterally.

Extensor indicis.name: Extensor indicis
Extensor indicis.fact: Extends the index finger independently (pointing) and assists wrist extension.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Extensor indicis is supplied by the PIN (C7-C8).

rel.q: The indicated muscle independently extends which digit?
rel.explain: It inserts on the extensor expansion of the 2nd digit, enabling pointing.

Abductor pollicis brevis.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
Abductor pollicis brevis.fact: Abducts the thumb; used to test the recurrent branch of the median nerve.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
rel.explain: Thenar muscles are supplied by the recurrent (thenar) branch of the median nerve.

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: It abducts the thumb perpendicular to the palm.

Flexor pollicis brevis.name: Flexor pollicis brevis
Flexor pollicis brevis.fact: Flexes the thumb at the MCP; superficial head by recurrent median, deep head often by deep ulnar.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the superficial head of the indicated muscle?
answers: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
rel.explain: The superficial head is median-supplied; the deep head often receives deep ulnar fibers.

rel.q: The indicated muscle flexes the thumb at which joint?
rel.explain: It inserts on the base of the proximal phalanx, flexing the MCP.

Opponens pollicis.name: Opponens pollicis
Opponens pollicis.fact: Opposes the thumb by flexing and medially rotating the 1st metacarpal.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
rel.explain: Opponens pollicis is supplied by the recurrent branch of the median nerve.

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: It rotates the 1st metacarpal to bring the thumb pad to the fingers.

Thumb adductor: Adductor pollicis.name: Adductor pollicis
Thumb adductor: Adductor pollicis.fact: Adducts the thumb for pinch grip; weakness gives a positive Froment sign; supplied by the deep palmar arch.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
rel.explain: Adductor pollicis is supplied by the deep ulnar branch (C8-T1).

rel.q: Weakness of the indicated muscle produces which clinical sign during pinch?
rel.explain: Patients flex the thumb IP (FPL, median) to compensate for lost adduction.

Abductor digiti minimi.name: Abductor digiti minimi
Abductor digiti minimi.fact: Abducts the 5th digit; arises from the pisiform and FCU tendon.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
rel.explain: Hypothenar muscles are supplied by the deep ulnar branch (C8-T1).

rel.q: The indicated muscle originates from which carpal bone?
rel.explain: ADM arises from the pisiform and FCU tendon.

Flexor digiti minimi brevis.name: Flexor digiti minimi brevis
Flexor digiti minimi brevis.fact: Flexes the 5th digit at the MCP joint; arises from the hook of hamate and flexor retinaculum.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
rel.explain: Hypothenar muscles are supplied by the deep ulnar branch (C8-T1).

Opponens digiti minimi.name: Opponens digiti minimi
Opponens digiti minimi.fact: Draws the 5th metacarpal anteriorly and rotates it toward the thumb.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
rel.explain: Hypothenar muscles are supplied by the deep ulnar branch (C8-T1).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which bone?
rel.explain: It inserts along the medial border of the 5th metacarpal.

Lumbricals.name: Lumbricals
Lumbricals.fact: Flex MCP and extend IP joints of digits 2-5; arise from FDP tendons; 1st-2nd median, 3rd-4th deep ulnar.

rel.q: The indicated muscles arise from the tendons of which forearm muscle?
rel.explain: Lumbricals originate from the FDP tendons in the palm.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the 1st and 2nd (lateral) muscles of this group?
rel.explain: Lateral two lumbricals: median; medial two: deep branch of ulnar.

Dorsal interossei.name: Dorsal interossei
Dorsal interossei.fact: Abduct digits from the 3rd-digit axis (DAB); assist MCP flexion and IP extension.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscles?
answers: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
rel.explain: All interossei are supplied by the deep ulnar branch (C8-T1).

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscles on the digits?
rel.explain: DAB: dorsal interossei abduct away from the 3rd-digit axis.

Palmar interossei.name: Palmar interossei
Palmar interossei.fact: Adduct digits 2, 4, 5 toward the 3rd-digit axis (PAD); assist MCP flexion and IP extension.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscles?
answers: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
rel.explain: All interossei are supplied by the deep ulnar branch (C8-T1).

rel.q: What is the main action of the indicated muscles on the digits?
rel.explain: PAD: palmar interossei adduct toward the 3rd-digit axis.

Anterior interosseous nerve.name: Anterior interosseous nerve
Anterior interosseous nerve.fact: Motor to FPL, lateral FDP, and pronator quadratus; no cutaneous branch; lesion prevents the OK sign.

rel.q: The indicated nerve is a branch of which nerve?
rel.explain: The AIN arises from the median nerve near pronator teres.

rel.q: Name a muscle innervated by the indicated nerve.
rel.show: FPL, pronator quadratus, or lateral FDP
rel.explain: AIN supplies FPL, lateral half of FDP, and pronator quadratus.

rel.q: Which artery accompanies the indicated nerve on the interosseous membrane?
rel.explain: AIN and anterior interosseous artery descend together on the membrane.

Posterior interosseous nerve.name: Posterior interosseous nerve
Posterior interosseous nerve.fact: Supplies the posterior forearm extensors; lesion causes finger drop without sensory loss.

rel.q: The indicated nerve is the continuation of which nerve?
answers: Deep branch of the radial nerve
rel.explain: The deep radial branch becomes the PIN after exiting the supinator.

rel.q: Which artery accompanies the indicated nerve?
rel.explain: PIN runs between superficial and deep extensors with the posterior interosseous artery.

rel.q: Name a muscle innervated by the indicated nerve.
rel.explain: PIN supplies ED, EDM, ECU, APL, EPB, EPL, and extensor indicis.

Radial artery.name: Radial artery
Radial artery.fact: Terminal branch of the brachial artery; wrist pulse; crosses the anatomical snuffbox and forms the deep palmar arch.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a terminal branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The brachial artery divides into radial and ulnar arteries in the cubital fossa.

rel.q: The indicated artery mainly forms which palmar arch?
rel.explain: The radial artery forms the deep arch, completed by the deep palmar branch of ulnar.

rel.q: The indicated artery crosses the floor of which space at the wrist?
rel.explain: It passes over the scaphoid and trapezium in the snuffbox.

Ulnar artery.name: Ulnar artery
Ulnar artery.fact: Larger terminal branch of the brachial artery; gives the common interosseous and forms the superficial palmar arch.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a terminal branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The brachial artery divides into radial and ulnar arteries in the cubital fossa.

rel.q: The indicated artery mainly forms which palmar arch?
rel.explain: The ulnar artery forms the superficial arch, completed by the superficial palmar branch of radial.

rel.q: The indicated artery enters the hand through which canal?
rel.explain: It passes with the ulnar nerve between pisiform and hook of hamate.

Anterior interosseous artery.name: Anterior interosseous artery
Anterior interosseous artery.fact: Runs on the anterior interosseous membrane with the AIN, supplying FPL, FDP, pronator quadratus, radius, and ulna.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The common interosseous divides into anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.

rel.q: Which nerve accompanies the indicated artery?
rel.explain: Both descend on the anterior surface of the interosseous membrane.

Posterior interosseous artery.name: Posterior interosseous artery
Posterior interosseous artery.fact: Supplies the extensor compartment, running between superficial and deep extensors with the PIN.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The common interosseous divides into anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.

rel.q: Which nerve accompanies the indicated artery?
rel.explain: They run together between the superficial and deep extensor layers.

rel.q: Which recurrent artery to the elbow arises from the indicated artery?
rel.explain: It ascends to the posterolateral elbow anastomosis.

Superficial palmar arch.name: Superficial palmar arch
Superficial palmar arch.fact: Formed mainly by the ulnar artery; lies deep to the palmar aponeurosis, distal to the deep arch; gives common palmar digital arteries.

rel.q: Which artery is the main contributor to the indicated structure?
rel.explain: Completed by the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery.

rel.q: The indicated structure gives off which arteries to the fingers?
rel.explain: Common palmar digital arteries split into proper digital arteries.

Deep palmar arch.name: Deep palmar arch
Deep palmar arch.fact: Formed mainly by the radial artery on the metacarpal bases, proximal to the superficial arch; gives palmar metacarpal arteries.

rel.q: Which artery is the main contributor to the indicated structure?
rel.explain: Completed by the deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery.

rel.q: The indicated structure gives off which arteries?
rel.explain: Palmar metacarpal arteries supply the interossei and join the common digitals.

Iliac fossa.name: Iliac fossa
Iliac fossa.fact: Smooth concave inner surface of the iliac ala forming the posterolateral wall of the greater pelvis.

rel.q: Name the muscle that arises from the indicated surface.
rel.explain: Iliacus originates from the iliac fossa and joins psoas major to insert on the lesser trochanter.

Iliac crest.name: Iliac crest
Iliac crest.fact: Palpable superior border of the ilium from ASIS to PSIS; its highest point marks L4 (lumbar puncture landmark).

rel.q: The highest point of the indicated structure lies at which vertebral level?
rel.explain: The supracristal plane through the highest points of the iliac crests crosses the L4 spinous process.

Anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS).name: Anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS)
Anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS).fact: Palpable anterior end of the iliac crest; attachment of sartorius, TFL and the lateral end of the inguinal ligament.

rel.q: Name a muscle that arises from the indicated landmark.
rel.explain: Sartorius and tensor fasciae latae both originate at the ASIS.

rel.q: Which ligament attaches laterally to the indicated landmark?
rel.explain: The inguinal ligament spans from the ASIS to the pubic tubercle.

Anterior inferior iliac spine (AIIS).name: Anterior inferior iliac spine (AIIS)
Anterior inferior iliac spine (AIIS).fact: Projection on the anterior ilium above the acetabulum; origin of the straight head of rectus femoris and of the iliofemoral ligament.

rel.q: Which muscle's straight head arises from the indicated landmark?
rel.explain: The straight head of rectus femoris arises from the AIIS; avulsion occurs with forceful kicking.

Ischial spine.name: Ischial spine
Ischial spine.fact: Separates the greater and lesser sciatic notches; landmark for pudendal nerve block.

rel.q: Which nerve passes just posterior to the indicated landmark and is blocked here?
rel.explain: The pudendal nerve crosses behind the ischial spine/sacrospinous ligament, the landmark for pudendal block.

rel.q: Which ligament attaches to the indicated landmark, separating the greater and lesser sciatic foramina?
rel.explain: The sacrospinous ligament runs from sacrum/coccyx to the ischial spine, dividing the two sciatic foramina.

Ischial tuberosity.name: Ischial tuberosity
Ischial tuberosity.fact: Weight-bearing 'sit bone' and common origin of the hamstrings.

rel.q: Name a muscle that arises from the indicated landmark.
rel.explain: The hamstrings, hamstring part of adductor magnus, quadratus femoris and inferior gemellus arise from the ischial tuberosity.

Superior pubic ramus.name: Superior pubic ramus
Superior pubic ramus.fact: Upper border of the obturator foramen carrying the pectineal line; the obturator canal lies beneath it.

rel.q: Which muscle arises from the pectineal line of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: Pectineus runs from the pectineal line of the superior pubic ramus to the pectineal line of the femur.

rel.q: Which canal lies immediately beneath the indicated structure?
rel.explain: The obturator canal is the gap under the superior pubic ramus not closed by the obturator membrane.

Inferior pubic ramus.name: Inferior pubic ramus
Inferior pubic ramus.fact: Joins the ischial ramus below the obturator foramen to form the ischiopubic ramus and pubic arch.

rel.q: Name a muscle that arises from the indicated structure.
rel.explain: Adductor brevis, gracilis, adductor magnus and obturator externus arise from the inferior pubic ramus.

Pubic tubercle.name: Pubic tubercle
Pubic tubercle.fact: Palpable anterior pubic projection; medial attachment of the inguinal ligament.

rel.q: Which ligament attaches to the indicated landmark?
rel.explain: The inguinal ligament runs from the ASIS to the pubic tubercle.

Pubic symphysis.name: Pubic symphysis
Pubic symphysis.fact: Secondary cartilaginous joint uniting the pubic bodies via a fibrocartilaginous disc; widens in pregnancy.

rel.q: What type of joint is the indicated structure?
rel.explain: The pubic symphysis is a symphysis (secondary cartilaginous joint) with a fibrocartilaginous interpubic disc.

Greater sciatic notch.name: Greater sciatic notch
Greater sciatic notch.fact: Notch above the ischial spine converted into the greater sciatic foramen by the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments.

rel.q: Which muscle exits the pelvis through the foramen formed from the indicated notch?
rel.explain: Piriformis passes through the greater sciatic foramen, dividing it into supra- and infrapiriform parts.

Lesser sciatic notch.name: Lesser sciatic notch
Lesser sciatic notch.fact: Notch below the ischial spine that becomes the lesser sciatic foramen.

rel.q: The tendon of which muscle turns over the indicated notch?
rel.explain: The obturator internus tendon bends ~90 degrees over the cartilage-covered lesser sciatic notch.

Obturator foramen.name: Obturator foramen
Obturator foramen.fact: Opening between pubis and ischium closed by the obturator membrane except for the obturator canal.

rel.q: Which nerve leaves the pelvis through the canal at the top of the indicated opening?
rel.explain: The obturator nerve and vessels pass through the obturator canal at the superior margin of the obturator foramen.

Acetabulum.name: Acetabulum
Acetabulum.fact: Deep cup-shaped socket formed by ilium, ischium and pubis that receives the femoral head.

rel.q: Name a bone that contributes to the indicated structure.
rel.explain: The ilium, ischium and pubis fuse at the Y-shaped triradiate cartilage to form the acetabulum.

rel.q: What articulates with the indicated structure?
rel.explain: The acetabulum and femoral head form the ball-and-socket hip joint.

Head of femur.name: Head of femur
Head of femur.fact: Two-thirds of a sphere articulating with the acetabulum; fovea holds the ligament of the head.

rel.q: Which artery provides the main blood supply to the indicated structure?
rel.explain: Retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery are the principal supply of the femoral head.

rel.q: The indicated structure articulates with which part of the hip bone?
rel.explain: The femoral head sits in the acetabulum, forming the hip joint.

Neck of femur.name: Neck of femur
Neck of femur.fact: Joins head to shaft at about 125 degrees; displaced intracapsular fractures tear retinacular arteries causing avascular necrosis.

rel.q: A displaced fracture here tears branches of which artery, risking avascular necrosis of the head?
rel.explain: Retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral run along the neck to the head.

Greater trochanter.name: Greater trochanter
Greater trochanter.fact: Palpable lateral prominence; lever for the hip abductors and lateral rotators.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated landmark.
rel.explain: Gluteus medius/minimus, piriformis, obturator internus, gemelli (and obturator externus in the trochanteric fossa) attach to the greater trochanter.

Lesser trochanter.name: Lesser trochanter
Lesser trochanter.fact: Posteromedial projection below the femoral neck; insertion of the principal hip flexor.

rel.q: Which muscle inserts on the indicated landmark?
rel.explain: Iliopsoas (psoas major and iliacus) inserts on the lesser trochanter.

Gluteus maximus.name: Gluteus maximus
Gluteus maximus.fact: Largest gluteal muscle; main hip extensor used in rising, climbing stairs and running.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The inferior gluteal nerve (L5-S2) exits below piriformis to supply gluteus maximus.

rel.q: Name the main action of the indicated muscle at the hip.
rel.explain: Gluteus maximus is the chief extensor of the hip.

Gluteus medius.name: Gluteus medius
Gluteus medius.fact: Abducts and medially rotates the thigh; keeps the pelvis level during single-leg stance.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1) runs between gluteus medius and minimus, supplying both.

rel.q: Weakness of the indicated muscle produces which clinical sign?
rel.explain: Without medius/minimus the pelvis drops on the unsupported side in single-leg stance.

Gluteus minimus.name: Gluteus minimus
Gluteus minimus.fact: Deepest gluteal muscle; abducts and medially rotates the thigh and stabilizes the pelvis with gluteus medius.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1) supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and TFL.

rel.q: Name the main action of the indicated muscle at the hip.
rel.explain: Gluteus minimus abducts (and medially rotates) the thigh.

Tensor fasciae latae.name: Tensor fasciae latae
Tensor fasciae latae.fact: Arises from the ASIS and tenses the iliotibial tract; abducts, medially rotates and flexes the hip.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: TFL is supplied by the superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts into which structure?
rel.explain: TFL inserts into the iliotibial tract, which continues to Gerdy tubercle.

Piriformis.name: Piriformis
Piriformis.fact: Key gluteal landmark passing through the greater sciatic foramen; laterally rotates the extended thigh.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Piriformis is supplied by the nerve to piriformis (S1-S2) on its pelvic surface.

rel.q: Through which opening does the indicated muscle leave the pelvis?
rel.explain: Piriformis exits the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen to reach the greater trochanter.

rel.q: Which large nerve can be compressed by the indicated muscle (piriformis syndrome)?
rel.explain: The sciatic nerve exits beneath piriformis and can be compressed by it.

Obturator internus.name: Obturator internus
Obturator internus.fact: Lateral rotator arising inside the pelvis whose tendon turns through the lesser sciatic foramen to the greater trochanter.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The nerve to obturator internus (L5-S2) enters the muscle's pelvic surface via the lesser sciatic foramen.

rel.q: Through which opening does the tendon of the indicated muscle leave the pelvis?
rel.explain: The obturator internus tendon exits via the lesser sciatic foramen, turning over the lesser sciatic notch.

Superior gemellus.name: Superior gemellus
Superior gemellus.fact: Small lateral rotator from the ischial spine reinforcing the obturator internus tendon.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Superior gemellus shares the nerve to obturator internus (L5-S2).

rel.q: The indicated muscle blends with the tendon of which muscle?
rel.explain: Both gemelli flank and insert with the obturator internus tendon onto the greater trochanter.

Inferior gemellus.name: Inferior gemellus
Inferior gemellus.fact: Small lateral rotator from the upper ischial tuberosity reinforcing the obturator internus tendon.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Inferior gemellus is supplied by the nerve to quadratus femoris (L4-S1).

rel.q: The indicated muscle blends with the tendon of which muscle?
rel.explain: Both gemelli flank and insert with the obturator internus tendon onto the greater trochanter.

Quadratus femoris.name: Quadratus femoris
