Quadratus femoris.fact: Strong lateral rotator from the ischial tuberosity to the quadrate tubercle of the intertrochanteric crest.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The nerve to quadratus femoris (L4-S1) supplies it and the inferior gemellus.

rel.q: Which artery runs deep to the indicated muscle and supplies it?
rel.explain: Quadratus femoris is supplied by the medial circumflex femoral artery.

Obturator externus.name: Obturator externus
Obturator externus.fact: Lateral rotator from the outer obturator membrane to the trochanteric fossa; medial-compartment muscle that does not adduct.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Obturator externus is supplied by the obturator nerve (L3-L4).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts into which part of the femur?
rel.explain: Obturator externus winds under the femoral neck to the trochanteric fossa.

Sartorius.name: Sartorius
Sartorius.fact: Longest muscle, ASIS to pes anserinus; flexes, abducts, laterally rotates the thigh and flexes the knee; roof of the adductor canal.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Sartorius is an anterior compartment muscle supplied by the femoral nerve (L2-L3).

rel.q: From which bony landmark does the indicated muscle arise?
rel.explain: Sartorius arises from the ASIS and inserts on the superomedial tibia (pes anserinus).

Rectus femoris.name: Rectus femoris
Rectus femoris.fact: Only quadriceps head crossing the hip: flexes the hip and extends the knee.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: All quadriceps heads are supplied by the femoral nerve (L2-L4).

rel.q: From which bony landmark does the straight head of the indicated muscle arise?
rel.explain: The straight head arises from the AIIS; the reflected head from above the acetabulum.

Vastus lateralis.name: Vastus lateralis
Vastus lateralis.fact: Largest quadriceps head on the lateral thigh; extends the knee; infant IM injection site.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: All quadriceps heads are supplied by the femoral nerve (L2-L4).

rel.q: Name the main action of the indicated muscle.
rel.explain: The vasti extend the knee via the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament.

Vastus medialis.name: Vastus medialis
Vastus medialis.fact: Medial quadriceps head; its oblique lower fibers pull the patella medially, resisting lateral dislocation.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: All quadriceps heads are supplied by the femoral nerve (L2-L4).

rel.q: Name the main action of the indicated muscle.
rel.explain: The vasti extend the knee via the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament.

Vastus intermedius.name: Vastus intermedius
Vastus intermedius.fact: Quadriceps head lying deep to rectus femoris on the anterior and lateral femoral shaft; extends the knee.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: All quadriceps heads are supplied by the femoral nerve (L2-L4).

rel.q: Which quadriceps muscle lies directly superficial to the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Vastus intermedius lies on the femoral shaft deep to rectus femoris.

Adductor brevis.name: Adductor brevis
Adductor brevis.fact: Adducts the thigh; the anterior and posterior divisions of the obturator nerve lie on either side of it.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Medial compartment adductors are supplied by the obturator nerve (L2-L4).

Adductor longus.name: Adductor longus
Adductor longus.fact: Superficial adductor from the pubic body to the middle linea aspera; groin strain muscle.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Medial compartment adductors are supplied by the obturator nerve (L2-L4).

rel.q: The medial border of the indicated muscle forms the medial border of which region?
rel.explain: Femoral triangle borders: inguinal ligament, sartorius, and the medial border of adductor longus.

Adductor magnus.name: Adductor magnus
Adductor magnus.fact: Largest adductor with an adductor part (obturator nerve) and hamstring part (tibial division of sciatic).

rel.q: What opening lies between the two distal attachments of the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The adductor hiatus lies between the aponeurotic and tendinous insertions of adductor magnus.

rel.q: Name the main action of the indicated muscle.
rel.explain: Adductor magnus is the largest adductor of the thigh.

Adductor part of adductor magnus.name: Adductor part of adductor magnus
Adductor part of adductor magnus.fact: Pubofemoral portion of adductor magnus from the ischiopubic ramus to the linea aspera; adducts the thigh.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The adductor part of adductor magnus is supplied by the obturator nerve (L2-L4).

Adductor canal.name: Adductor canal
Adductor canal.fact: Passage from the femoral triangle apex to the adductor hiatus carrying femoral vessels, saphenous nerve and nerve to vastus medialis.

rel.q: Which muscle forms the roof of the indicated canal?
rel.explain: Sartorius covers the vastoadductor membrane that roofs the adductor canal.

rel.q: Through which opening does the femoral artery leave the indicated canal?
rel.explain: The femoral vessels exit via the adductor hiatus to become the popliteal vessels.

rel.q: Which cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve travels through the indicated canal?
rel.explain: The saphenous nerve accompanies the femoral artery in the adductor canal.

Gracilis.name: Gracilis
Gracilis.fact: Thin medial strap muscle from the pubis to pes anserinus; adducts the thigh and flexes the knee; expendable graft muscle.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Gracilis is a medial compartment muscle supplied by the obturator nerve (L2-L3).

Pectineus.name: Pectineus
Pectineus.fact: Transitional muscle in the floor of the femoral triangle; adducts and flexes the thigh.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Pectineus is usually supplied by the femoral nerve (L2-L3), sometimes with an obturator branch.

Semitendinosus.name: Semitendinosus
Semitendinosus.fact: Hamstring with a long cord-like tendon to pes anserinus; extends hip, flexes knee.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
Tibial part of the sciatic nerve
rel.show: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
rel.explain: Hamstrings except the short head of biceps are supplied by the tibial division of the sciatic nerve.

rel.q: From which bony landmark does the indicated muscle arise?
rel.explain: Semitendinosus arises from the ischial tuberosity with the long head of biceps femoris.

Semimembranosus.name: Semimembranosus
Semimembranosus.fact: Medial hamstring inserting on the posterior medial tibial condyle; extends hip, flexes knee.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
Tibial part of the sciatic nerve
rel.show: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
rel.explain: Hamstrings except the short head of biceps are supplied by the tibial division of the sciatic nerve.

rel.q: From which bony landmark does the indicated muscle arise?
rel.explain: Semimembranosus arises from the ischial tuberosity.

Biceps femoris, long head.name: Biceps femoris, long head
Biceps femoris, long head.fact: Lateral hamstring from the ischial tuberosity to the fibular head; extends hip, flexes knee.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
answers: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
Tibial part of the sciatic nerve
rel.show: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
rel.explain: The long head is supplied by the tibial division; only the short head uses the common fibular division.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which bony landmark?
rel.explain: Both heads of biceps femoris insert on the head of the fibula.

Femoral nerve.name: Femoral nerve
Femoral nerve.fact: Lumbar plexus nerve (L2-L4) passing under the inguinal ligament lateral to the femoral artery; supplies the anterior thigh.

rel.q: Name a muscle innervated by the indicated nerve.
rel.explain: The femoral nerve supplies quadriceps, sartorius, pectineus and iliacus.

rel.q: Which cutaneous branch of the indicated nerve supplies the medial leg?
rel.explain: The saphenous nerve is the terminal cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve.

rel.q: The indicated nerve arises from which plexus?
rel.explain: The femoral nerve arises from the posterior divisions of L2-L4 of the lumbar plexus.

Obturator nerve.name: Obturator nerve
Obturator nerve.fact: Lumbar plexus nerve (L2-L4) leaving the pelvis through the obturator canal to supply the medial thigh adductors.

rel.q: Through which opening does the indicated nerve leave the pelvis?
rel.explain: The obturator nerve passes through the obturator canal into the medial thigh.

rel.q: Name a muscle innervated by the indicated nerve.
rel.explain: The obturator nerve supplies the medial compartment adductors, gracilis and obturator externus.

Sciatic nerve.name: Sciatic nerve
Sciatic nerve.fact: Largest nerve (L4-S3); exits below piriformis and splits into tibial and common fibular nerves at the popliteal apex.

rel.q: The indicated nerve usually exits the greater sciatic foramen below which muscle?
rel.explain: The sciatic nerve emerges inferior to piriformis.

rel.q: Name a muscle of the thigh innervated by the indicated nerve.
rel.explain: In the thigh the sciatic supplies the hamstrings and hamstring part of adductor magnus.

rel.q: The indicated nerve arises from which plexus?
rel.explain: The sciatic nerve is the main branch of the sacral plexus (L4-S3).

Medial condyle of femur.name: Medial condyle of femur
Medial condyle of femur.fact: Larger medial articular condyle of the distal femur; PCL attaches to its notch surface.

rel.q: Which cruciate ligament attaches to the intercondylar surface of the indicated condyle?
rel.explain: The PCL runs to the anterolateral surface of the medial femoral condyle.

Lateral condyle of femur.name: Lateral condyle of femur
Lateral condyle of femur.fact: Lateral articular condyle of the distal femur; ACL attaches to its notch surface.

rel.q: Which cruciate ligament attaches to the intercondylar surface of the indicated condyle?
rel.explain: The ACL runs to the posteromedial surface of the lateral femoral condyle.

Patellar surface of the femur.name: Patellar surface of the femur
Patellar surface of the femur.fact: Anterior grooved articular surface whose prominent lateral lip resists lateral patellar dislocation.

rel.q: Which bone articulates with the indicated surface?
rel.explain: The patellar surface forms the patellofemoral joint with the patella.

Intercondylar fossa of the femur.name: Intercondylar fossa of the femur
Intercondylar fossa of the femur.fact: Deep notch between the femoral condyles housing the cruciate ligaments.

rel.q: Name a ligament that attaches within the indicated fossa.
rel.explain: Both cruciate ligaments attach to the walls of the intercondylar fossa.

Tibia.name: Tibia
Tibia.fact: Medial weight-bearing bone of the leg transmitting body weight from femur to talus.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates distally with which bone?
rel.explain: The distal tibia and medial malleolus articulate with the talus at the ankle.

Patella.name: Patella
Patella.fact: Largest sesamoid bone, within the quadriceps tendon; increases the extensor lever arm.

rel.q: The indicated bone develops within the tendon of which muscle?
rel.explain: The patella is a sesamoid bone in the quadriceps tendon.

rel.q: What type of bone is the indicated bone?
rel.explain: The patella is the body's largest sesamoid bone.

Fibula.name: Fibula
Fibula.fact: Slender non-weight-bearing lateral leg bone; not part of the knee joint.

rel.q: Which nerve winds around the neck of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: The common fibular nerve wraps the fibular neck; injury there causes foot drop.

rel.q: Which thigh muscle inserts on the head of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: Both heads of biceps femoris insert on the fibular head.

Medial meniscus.name: Medial meniscus
Medial meniscus.fact: C-shaped, less mobile meniscus fused to the tibial collateral ligament; torn more often (unhappy triad).

rel.q: Which collateral ligament is attached to the indicated structure?
rel.explain: The medial meniscus is fused to the tibial collateral ligament, so they tear together.

Lateral meniscus.name: Lateral meniscus
Lateral meniscus.fact: Nearly circular, more mobile meniscus separated from the fibular collateral ligament by the popliteus tendon.

rel.q: Which muscle's tendon separates the indicated structure from the fibular collateral ligament?
rel.explain: The popliteus tendon intervenes, making the lateral meniscus more mobile.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL).name: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL).fact: Prevents anterior tibial displacement on the femur; torn in pivoting injuries; tested by Lachman and anterior drawer.

rel.q: The indicated ligament attaches to which femoral condyle?
rel.explain: The ACL runs from the anterior intercondylar tibia to the medial surface of the lateral femoral condyle.

rel.q: The indicated ligament prevents displacement of the tibia in which direction?
rel.explain: The ACL resists anterior translation of the tibia on the femur.

Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL).name: Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL)
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL).fact: Stronger cruciate preventing posterior tibial displacement; dashboard injury; posterior drawer test.

rel.q: The indicated ligament attaches to which femoral condyle?
rel.explain: The PCL runs from the posterior intercondylar tibia to the lateral surface of the medial femoral condyle.

rel.q: The indicated ligament prevents displacement of the tibia in which direction?
rel.explain: The PCL resists posterior translation of the tibia (dashboard injury).

Inguinal ligament.name: Inguinal ligament
Inguinal ligament.fact: Inrolled lower edge of the external oblique aponeurosis from ASIS to pubic tubercle; base of the femoral triangle.

rel.q: The indicated structure is formed by the aponeurosis of which muscle?
rel.explain: The inguinal ligament is the folded inferior edge of the external oblique aponeurosis.

rel.q: The indicated structure attaches medially to which landmark?
rel.explain: It spans from the ASIS laterally to the pubic tubercle medially.

Common iliac artery.name: Common iliac artery
Common iliac artery.fact: Terminal branch of the abdominal aorta that divides in front of the sacroiliac joint into internal and external iliac arteries.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The abdominal aorta bifurcates at L4 into the two common iliac arteries.

Internal iliac artery.name: Internal iliac artery
Internal iliac artery.fact: Supplies pelvic organs, perineum, gluteal region and medial thigh via anterior and posterior divisions.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The common iliac divides into internal and external iliac arteries at the sacroiliac joint.

rel.q: Name a branch of the indicated artery that leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen.
rel.explain: Superior gluteal, inferior gluteal and internal pudendal arteries exit via the greater sciatic foramen.

External iliac artery.name: External iliac artery
External iliac artery.fact: Main arterial supply to the lower limb, running along the pelvic brim on psoas.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The common iliac divides into internal and external iliac arteries at the sacroiliac joint.

rel.q: What does the indicated artery become after passing under the inguinal ligament?
rel.explain: Beneath the inguinal ligament the external iliac is renamed the femoral artery.

Superior gluteal artery.name: Superior gluteal artery
Superior gluteal artery.fact: Largest internal iliac branch; exits above piriformis with the superior gluteal nerve to supply gluteus medius, minimus and TFL.

rel.q: The indicated artery arises from which division of the internal iliac artery?
answers: Posterior division of the internal iliac artery
rel.show: Posterior division of the internal iliac
rel.explain: The superior gluteal is the main branch of the posterior division of the internal iliac.

rel.q: The indicated artery exits the greater sciatic foramen above which muscle?
rel.explain: It passes above piriformis with the superior gluteal nerve.

Inferior gluteal artery.name: Inferior gluteal artery
Inferior gluteal artery.fact: Anterior-division internal iliac branch exiting below piriformis to supply gluteus maximus and posterior thigh.

rel.q: The indicated artery arises from which division of the internal iliac artery?
answers: Anterior division of the internal iliac artery
rel.show: Anterior division of the internal iliac
rel.explain: The inferior gluteal is a branch of the anterior division of the internal iliac.

rel.q: The indicated artery exits the greater sciatic foramen below which muscle?
rel.explain: It passes below piriformis with the inferior gluteal nerve.

Obturator artery.name: Obturator artery
Obturator artery.fact: Internal iliac branch passing through the obturator canal to the medial thigh; gives the artery of the ligament of the head.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
answers: Anterior division of the internal iliac artery
rel.explain: The obturator artery arises from the anterior division of the internal iliac.

rel.q: Through which opening does the indicated artery leave the pelvis?
rel.explain: It accompanies the obturator nerve through the obturator canal.

Femoral artery (common and superficial).name: Femoral artery (common and superficial)
Femoral artery (common and superficial).fact: Continuation of the external iliac: 'common' above the profunda origin, 'superficial' below it through the adductor canal.

rel.q: The indicated artery is the continuation of which artery?
rel.explain: The external iliac becomes the femoral artery beneath the inguinal ligament.

rel.q: What does the indicated artery become after passing through the adductor hiatus?
rel.explain: At the adductor hiatus the femoral artery is renamed the popliteal artery.

rel.q: What is the largest branch of the indicated artery in the femoral triangle?
rel.explain: The deep femoral arises about 4 cm below the inguinal ligament.

Deep femoral artery (profunda femoris).name: Deep femoral artery (profunda femoris)
Deep femoral artery (profunda femoris).fact: Main supply of the thigh muscles and, via the circumflex femoral arteries, of the femoral head and neck.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The deep femoral arises from the femoral artery about 4 cm below the inguinal ligament.

rel.q: Name a branch of the indicated artery.
rel.explain: Branches: medial and lateral circumflex femoral and 3-4 perforating arteries.

Medial circumflex femoral artery.name: Medial circumflex femoral artery
Medial circumflex femoral artery.fact: Passes between pectineus and iliopsoas to the trochanteric fossa; principal supply of the femoral head via retinacular arteries.

rel.q: The indicated artery is usually a branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The medial circumflex femoral usually arises from the deep femoral (sometimes the femoral).

rel.q: Which structure receives its main blood supply from the indicated artery?
rel.explain: Its retinacular branches are the principal supply of the femoral head and neck.

Lateral circumflex femoral artery.name: Lateral circumflex femoral artery
Lateral circumflex femoral artery.fact: Runs laterally deep to sartorius and rectus femoris; ascending, transverse and descending branches supply anterior thigh.

rel.q: The indicated artery is usually a branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The lateral circumflex femoral usually arises from the deep femoral.

rel.q: The descending branch of the indicated artery runs along which muscle?
rel.explain: The descending branch runs on vastus lateralis, supplying it.

Popliteal artery.name: Popliteal artery
Popliteal artery.fact: Deepest structure of the popliteal fossa; gives genicular branches and divides at lower popliteus into anterior and posterior tibial arteries.

rel.q: The indicated artery is the continuation of which artery?
rel.explain: The femoral artery becomes the popliteal artery at the adductor hiatus.

rel.q: The vessel preceding the indicated artery passes through which opening to become it?
rel.explain: The femoral artery is renamed popliteal after passing the adductor hiatus.

Great saphenous vein.name: Great saphenous vein
Great saphenous vein.fact: Longest superficial vein, from the medial dorsal venous arch to the femoral vein; harvested for coronary bypass grafts.

rel.q: The indicated vein drains into which vein?
rel.explain: The great saphenous passes through the saphenous opening to join the femoral vein.

rel.q: The indicated vein passes anterior to which bony landmark at the ankle?
rel.explain: The great saphenous vein lies anterior to the medial malleolus, a reliable cutdown site.

Femoral vein.name: Femoral vein
Femoral vein.fact: Main deep vein of the thigh lying medial to the femoral artery in the femoral triangle; common DVT site.

rel.q: The indicated vein drains into which vein?
rel.explain: Under the inguinal ligament the femoral vein becomes the external iliac vein.

rel.q: Which superficial vein drains into the indicated vein in the femoral triangle?
rel.explain: The great saphenous enters the femoral vein via the saphenous opening.

rel.q: What vessel immediately precedes the indicated vein, continuing into it at the adductor hiatus?
rel.explain: The popliteal vein becomes the femoral vein at the adductor hiatus.

Popliteal vein.name: Popliteal vein
Popliteal vein.fact: Deep vein of the knee lying superficial to the popliteal artery; DVT here risks pulmonary embolism.

rel.q: The indicated vein drains into which vein?
rel.explain: The popliteal vein becomes the femoral vein at the adductor hiatus.

rel.q: Which superficial vein drains into the indicated vein?
rel.explain: The small saphenous vein ends in the popliteal vein.

External iliac vein.name: External iliac vein
External iliac vein.fact: Continuation of the femoral vein above the inguinal ligament; drains the lower limb.

rel.q: The indicated vein drains into which vein?
rel.explain: External and internal iliac veins unite to form the common iliac vein.

rel.q: What vessel immediately precedes the indicated vein?
rel.explain: The femoral vein becomes the external iliac vein beneath the inguinal ligament.

Internal iliac vein.name: Internal iliac vein
Internal iliac vein.fact: Drains pelvic organs, perineum and gluteal region.

rel.q: The indicated vein drains into which vein?
rel.explain: Internal and external iliac veins unite in front of the sacroiliac joint to form the common iliac vein.

Common iliac vein.name: Common iliac vein
Common iliac vein.fact: Formed by external and internal iliac veins; the two unite at L5 to form the IVC; left compressed in May-Thurner.

rel.q: The indicated vein drains into which vein?
rel.explain: The common iliac veins unite at L5 to form the inferior vena cava.

Head of fibula.name: Head of fibula
Head of fibula.fact: Palpable at the posterolateral knee; articulates with the lateral tibial condyle and receives biceps femoris and the fibular collateral ligament.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated landmark.
rel.explain: Biceps femoris inserts on the fibular head; fibularis longus and soleus arise from it.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates proximally with which bone?
rel.explain: The head of the fibula forms the proximal tibiofibular joint with the lateral tibial condyle; it does not reach the femur.

Lateral malleolus of Fibula.name: Lateral malleolus of Fibula
Lateral malleolus of Fibula.fact: Lateral wall of the ankle mortise, lower and more posterior than the medial malleolus; ATFL, CFL and PTFL attach and fibularis tendons groove behind it.

rel.q: Name a muscle whose tendon passes in the groove immediately posterior to the indicated landmark.
rel.explain: Fibularis brevis and longus tendons pass behind the lateral malleolus under the fibular retinacula.

rel.q: Which ligament runs from the tip of the indicated landmark to the lateral surface of the calcaneus?
rel.explain: The calcaneofibular ligament runs from the malleolar tip to the calcaneus, resisting inversion.

Body of talus.name: Body of talus
Body of talus.fact: Bulk of the talus carrying the trochlea; its posterior process is grooved by the FHL tendon and no muscles attach to the talus.

rel.q: Which tendon runs in the groove on the posterior process of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: FHL tendon grooves the posterior talar process between medial and lateral tubercles, then passes under the sustentaculum tali.

rel.q: The inferior surface of the indicated bone articulates with which bone?
rel.explain: The inferior facets of the talus articulate with the calcaneus at the subtalar joint.

Trochlea of talus.name: Trochlea of talus
Trochlea of talus.fact: Superior articular surface of the talocrural joint; wider anteriorly, so the ankle is most stable in dorsiflexion.

rel.q: The indicated articular surface articulates superiorly with which bone?
rel.explain: The trochlea articulates with the tibial plafond above and both malleoli at the talocrural joint.

Calcaneus: Calcaneal tuberosity.name: Calcaneal tuberosity
Calcaneus: Calcaneal tuberosity.fact: The calcaneus is the largest tarsal; its tuberosity receives the calcaneal tendon and gives origin to the plantar aponeurosis and superficial sole muscles.

rel.q: Name a muscle that attaches to the indicated landmark.
rel.explain: Triceps surae and plantaris insert here; abductor hallucis, FDB and ADM arise from the tuberosity.

rel.q: Which tendon inserts on the posterior surface of the indicated landmark?
rel.explain: The calcaneal (Achilles) tendon inserts on the middle of the posterior calcaneal tuberosity.

Navicular.name: Navicular
Navicular.fact: Its tuberosity is the main insertion of tibialis posterior; the spring ligament attaches to its plantar surface.

rel.q: Which muscle has its main insertion on the tuberosity of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: Tibialis posterior inserts chiefly on the navicular tuberosity, with slips to cuneiforms, cuboid and MT2-4.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates proximally with which bone?
rel.explain: The navicular articulates with the talar head proximally (talonavicular joint) and the three cuneiforms distally.

Cuboid.name: Cuboid
Cuboid.fact: Keystone of the lateral longitudinal arch; its plantar groove carries the fibularis longus tendon.

rel.q: Which tendon runs in the groove on the plantar surface of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: The fibularis longus tendon crosses the sole in the cuboid groove, roofed by the long plantar ligament.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates proximally with which bone?
rel.explain: The cuboid forms the calcaneocuboid joint proximally and articulates with MT4-5 distally.

Medial cuneiform.name: Medial cuneiform
Medial cuneiform.fact: Largest cuneiform, part of the medial column; tibialis anterior and fibularis longus both insert here.

rel.q: Name a muscle that inserts on the indicated bone.
rel.explain: Tibialis anterior and fibularis longus both insert on the medial cuneiform and MT1 base (tibialis posterior sends a slip).

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates distally with which bone?
rel.explain: The medial cuneiform articulates with the base of the first metatarsal.

Intermediate cuneiform.name: Intermediate cuneiform
Intermediate cuneiform.fact: Smallest cuneiform; recessed so the MT2 base keys in between neighbors, locking the Lisfranc joint.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates distally with which bone?
rel.explain: The intermediate cuneiform articulates with the base of the second metatarsal.

Lateral cuneiform.name: Lateral cuneiform
Lateral cuneiform.fact: Wedge between the intermediate cuneiform and cuboid; articulates with the navicular and the base of MT3.

rel.q: The indicated bone articulates distally with which bone?
rel.explain: The lateral cuneiform articulates with the base of the third metatarsal.

Metatarsal I.name: Metatarsal I
Metatarsal I.fact: Shortest, thickest metatarsal; its head carries two sesamoids and bears much push-off load.

rel.q: Name a muscle that inserts on the base of the indicated bone.
rel.explain: Both tibialis anterior and fibularis longus insert on the medial cuneiform and base of MT1.

rel.q: The base of the indicated bone articulates with which tarsal bone?
rel.explain: MT1 articulates proximally with the medial cuneiform.

Metatarsal II.name: Metatarsal II
Metatarsal II.fact: Longest metatarsal; its base is keyed between the cuneiforms and it is the commonest site of stress (march) fracture.

rel.q: Which ligament ties the base of the indicated bone to the medial cuneiform?
rel.explain: The Lisfranc ligament binds the medial cuneiform to the MT2 base, stabilizing the tarsometatarsal joint.

Metatarsal III.name: Metatarsal III
Metatarsal III.fact: Central ray of the forefoot; stress fractures are also common here.

rel.q: The base of the indicated bone articulates with which tarsal bone?
rel.explain: MT3's base articulates with the lateral cuneiform.

Metatarsal IV.name: Metatarsal IV
Metatarsal IV.fact: Part of the lateral column; its base articulates with the cuboid.

rel.q: The base of the indicated bone articulates with which tarsal bone?
rel.explain: MT4 and MT5 both articulate proximally with the cuboid.

Metatarsal V.name: Metatarsal V
Metatarsal V.fact: Lateral column; its tuberosity receives fibularis brevis and is the site of avulsion and Jones fractures.

rel.q: Which muscle inserts on the tuberosity at the base of the indicated bone?
rel.explain: Fibularis brevis inserts on the MT5 tuberosity; its pull explains tuberosity avulsion fractures.

rel.q: The base of the indicated bone articulates with which tarsal bone?
rel.explain: MT5 articulates proximally with the cuboid.

Tibialis anterior.name: Tibialis anterior
Tibialis anterior.fact: Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot; from the lateral tibia and interosseous membrane to the medial cuneiform and MT1 base.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: All anterior compartment muscles are supplied by the deep fibular nerve (L4-L5 here).

rel.q: Which artery supplies the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The anterior tibial artery runs with the deep fibular nerve on the interosseous membrane supplying the anterior compartment.

rel.q: Name a bone on which the indicated muscle inserts.
rel.explain: Tibialis anterior inserts on the medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal.

Extensor hallucis longus.name: Extensor hallucis longus
Extensor hallucis longus.fact: Extends the great toe and dorsiflexes the foot; inserts on the base of the hallux distal phalanx.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: EHL is an anterior compartment muscle, supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

rel.q: Which artery's pulse is palpated just lateral to the tendon of the indicated muscle on the dorsum of the foot?
rel.explain: The dorsalis pedis pulse is felt lateral to the EHL tendon over the navicular/cuneiforms.

Extensor digitorum longus.name: Extensor digitorum longus
Extensor digitorum longus.fact: Extends the lateral four toes and dorsiflexes the foot via extensor expansions onto middle and distal phalanges II-V.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: EDL is an anterior compartment muscle, supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

rel.q: Which artery supplies the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The anterior tibial artery supplies the anterior compartment.

Fibularis tertius.name: Fibularis tertius
Fibularis tertius.fact: Dorsiflexes and everts the foot; from the distal anterior fibula to the dorsum of the MT5 base.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Despite its name, fibularis tertius sits in the anterior compartment and is supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on the dorsum of the base of which bone?
rel.explain: Fibularis tertius inserts on the dorsal base of MT5.

Fibularis longus.name: Fibularis longus
Fibularis longus.fact: Everts and plantarflexes the foot; its tendon crosses the sole in the cuboid groove to the medial cuneiform and MT1 base.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Lateral compartment muscles (fibularis longus and brevis) are supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.

rel.q: The tendon of the indicated muscle crosses the sole in a groove on which tarsal bone?
rel.explain: The fibularis longus tendon runs in the plantar groove of the cuboid, under the long plantar ligament.

rel.q: Name a bone on which the indicated muscle inserts.
rel.explain: Fibularis longus inserts on the medial cuneiform and base of MT1.

Fibularis brevis.name: Fibularis brevis
Fibularis brevis.fact: Everts the foot with weak plantarflexion; from the lower lateral fibula to the tuberosity of the MT5 base.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Fibularis brevis is a lateral compartment muscle, supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on the tuberosity of which bone?
rel.explain: Fibularis brevis inserts on the MT5 tuberosity.

Gastrocnemius.name: Gastrocnemius
Gastrocnemius.fact: Plantarflexes the ankle and flexes the knee; arises from both femoral condyles and inserts via the calcaneal tendon.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: All posterior leg compartment muscles are supplied by the tibial nerve (S1-S2 for gastrocnemius).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which bony landmark?
rel.explain: Gastrocnemius inserts via the calcaneal tendon on the calcaneal tuberosity.

rel.q: Which artery gives the sural arteries supplying the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The sural arteries arise from the popliteal artery in the popliteal fossa.

Soleus.name: Soleus
Soleus.fact: Postural plantarflexor and calf venous pump; arises from the fibular head and soleal line of the tibia.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Soleus, in the superficial posterior compartment, is supplied by the tibial nerve (S1-S2).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts on which bony landmark?
rel.explain: Soleus joins gastrocnemius in the calcaneal tendon to the calcaneal tuberosity.

Plantaris.name: Plantaris
Plantaris.fact: Small vestigial plantarflexor/knee flexor from the lateral supracondylar line; its long thin tendon is used as a graft.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Plantaris is in the superficial posterior compartment, supplied by the tibial nerve.

rel.q: The indicated muscle arises from which bone?
rel.explain: Plantaris arises from the lateral supracondylar line of the femur.

Calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.name: Calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
Calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.fact: Transmits triceps surae pull for plantarflexion; tested by the ankle jerk reflex (S1-S2); rupture weakens push-off.

rel.q: Name a muscle that contributes to the indicated tendon.
rel.explain: The calcaneal tendon is the common tendon of gastrocnemius and soleus (triceps surae).

rel.q: Tapping the indicated tendon tests which spinal cord level?
rel.explain: The ankle jerk reflex is mediated mainly by S1 (S1-S2) via the tibial nerve.

Tibialis posterior.name: Tibialis posterior
Tibialis posterior.fact: Inverts and plantarflexes the foot and is the main dynamic support of the medial longitudinal arch.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Tibialis posterior, deep posterior compartment, is supplied by the tibial nerve (L4-L5).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts mainly on the tuberosity of which bone?
rel.explain: Tibialis posterior inserts chiefly on the navicular tuberosity.

Flexor digitorum longus.name: Flexor digitorum longus
Flexor digitorum longus.fact: Flexes the lateral four toes and assists plantarflexion/inversion; inserts on bases of distal phalanges II-V.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FDL is a deep posterior compartment muscle, supplied by the tibial nerve.

rel.q: Which intrinsic sole muscle inserts on the tendon of the indicated muscle to straighten its pull?
rel.explain: Quadratus plantae attaches to the lateral margin of the FDL tendon, correcting its oblique pull.

Flexor hallucis longus.name: Flexor hallucis longus
Flexor hallucis longus.fact: Flexes the great toe for push-off and supports the medial arch; from the lower posterior fibula to the hallux distal phalanx.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FHL is a deep posterior compartment muscle, supplied by the tibial nerve.

rel.q: The indicated muscle arises mainly from which bone?
rel.explain: Despite inserting on the hallux, FHL arises laterally from the lower posterior fibula.

rel.q: Which artery supplies the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The fibular artery runs along the fibula near FHL and supplies it.

Deltoid ligament.name: Deltoid ligament
alts: Medial collateral ligament of the ankle
Deltoid ligament.fact: Strong medial ankle ligament resisting eversion; may avulse the medial malleolus rather than tear.

rel.q: The indicated ligament attaches proximally to which bony landmark?
rel.explain: The deltoid ligament fans from the medial malleolus to navicular, talus and sustentaculum tali.

rel.q: The indicated ligament mainly resists which movement of the foot?
rel.explain: The deltoid ligament on the medial side limits eversion.

Extensor digitorum brevis.name: Extensor digitorum brevis
Extensor digitorum brevis.fact: Dorsal foot muscle from the superolateral calcaneus that assists EDL in extending toes II-IV.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: The dorsal foot muscles (EDB, EHB) are supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

Extensor hallucis brevis.name: Extensor hallucis brevis
Extensor hallucis brevis.fact: Extends the great toe at the MTP joint; from the superolateral calcaneus to the base of the hallux proximal phalanx.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: EHB, like EDB, is supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

Abductor hallucis.name: Abductor hallucis
Abductor hallucis.fact: Abducts and flexes the great toe and supports the medial arch; plantar nerves and vessels pass deep to it.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Abductor hallucis is supplied by the medial plantar nerve (S2-S3).

rel.q: The indicated muscle arises from which bony landmark?
rel.explain: Abductor hallucis arises from the medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity and flexor retinaculum.

Flexor hallucis brevis.name: Flexor hallucis brevis
Flexor hallucis brevis.fact: Flexes the great toe at the MTP joint; its two tendons contain the hallux sesamoids.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FHB is supplied by the medial plantar nerve.

Flexor digitorum brevis.name: Flexor digitorum brevis
Flexor digitorum brevis.fact: Flexes the lateral four toes at the PIP joints; inserts on the sides of middle phalanges II-V.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FDB is supplied by the medial plantar nerve.

rel.q: The tendons of the indicated muscle insert on which phalanges of toes II-V?
rel.explain: FDB tendons split around FDL to insert on the middle phalanges.

Quadratus plantae.name: Quadratus plantae
Quadratus plantae.fact: Straightens the oblique pull of the FDL tendons, assisting toe flexion; arises from both sides of the plantar calcaneus.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: Quadratus plantae is supplied by the lateral plantar nerve.

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts onto the tendon of which muscle?
rel.explain: Quadratus plantae inserts on the posterolateral margin of the FDL tendon.

Flexor digit minimi brevis.name: Flexor digit minimi brevis
Flexor digit minimi brevis.fact: Flexes the little toe at the MTP joint; from the base of MT5 to the base of the proximal phalanx of toe V.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: FDMB is supplied by the superficial branch of the lateral plantar nerve.

rel.q: The indicated muscle arises from the base of which bone?
rel.explain: FDMB arises from the base of the fifth metatarsal.

Common fibular nerve.name: Common fibular nerve
Common fibular nerve.fact: Winds around the fibular neck to supply anterior and lateral compartments; injury there causes foot drop and steppage gait.

rel.q: The indicated nerve is a terminal branch of which nerve?
rel.explain: The sciatic nerve divides into the tibial and common fibular nerves, usually above the popliteal fossa.

rel.q: The indicated nerve wraps around which bony landmark, where it is vulnerable to injury?
rel.explain: Fibular neck fracture or cast compression injures the common fibular nerve.

rel.q: Injury to the indicated nerve classically produces what deficit?
rel.explain: Loss of anterior compartment dorsiflexors causes foot drop with a steppage gait.

Tibial nerve.name: Tibial nerve
Tibial nerve.fact: Supplies the posterior leg and (via plantar nerves) the sole; most superficial structure in the popliteal fossa.

rel.q: The indicated nerve is a terminal branch of which nerve?
rel.explain: The tibial nerve is the larger terminal division of the sciatic nerve.

rel.q: At the ankle the indicated nerve passes through which space?
rel.explain: It passes behind the medial malleolus through the tarsal tunnel, then divides into plantar nerves.

rel.q: Name a terminal branch of the indicated nerve.
rel.explain: In the tarsal tunnel the tibial nerve divides into medial and lateral plantar nerves.

Lateral plantar nerve.name: Lateral plantar nerve
Lateral plantar nerve.fact: Ulnar-nerve analog of the sole: supplies QP, ADM, FDMB, adductor hallucis, interossei and lumbricals 2-4, plus skin of lateral 1.5 toes.

rel.q: The indicated nerve is a terminal branch of which nerve?
rel.explain: The tibial nerve divides into medial and lateral plantar nerves in the tarsal tunnel.

rel.q: Name a muscle innervated by the indicated nerve.
rel.explain: Lateral plantar nerve supplies most intrinsic sole muscles, including QP, ADM, FDMB, adductor hallucis and interossei.

Anterior tibial artery.name: Anterior tibial artery
Anterior tibial artery.fact: Passes above the interosseous membrane into the anterior compartment, runs with the deep fibular nerve and becomes the dorsalis pedis.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The popliteal artery divides into anterior and posterior tibial arteries at the lower border of popliteus.

rel.q: What does the indicated artery become after crossing the ankle joint?
rel.explain: The anterior tibial artery continues as the dorsalis pedis on the dorsum of the foot.

rel.q: Which nerve accompanies the indicated artery?
rel.explain: The deep fibular nerve runs with the anterior tibial artery in the anterior compartment.

Posterior tibial artery.name: Posterior tibial artery
Posterior tibial artery.fact: Supplies the posterior compartment and sole; its pulse is felt behind the medial malleolus.

rel.q: The indicated artery is a direct branch of which artery?
rel.explain: The posterior tibial artery is a terminal branch of the popliteal artery.

rel.q: Name the major branch the indicated artery gives off just below popliteus.
rel.explain: The fibular artery arises from the posterior tibial artery just below popliteus.

rel.q: Name a terminal branch of the indicated artery.
rel.explain: In the tarsal tunnel it divides into medial and lateral plantar arteries.

Biceps brachii.name: Biceps brachii
Biceps brachii.fact: Two-headed anterior arm muscle: chief supinator of the forearm and a strong elbow flexor; inserts on the radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis.

rel.q: What nerve innervates the indicated muscle?
rel.explain: All anterior arm muscles are supplied by the musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C7).

rel.q: The indicated muscle inserts mainly on which bony landmark?
rel.explain: Its tendon inserts on the radial tuberosity, making it a powerful supinator.
